Offering distance learning as an option for students to attend classes from home by way of online or video conferencing by schools is a good idea, but I take a position on this issue to say that, students would not benefit from being able to attend classes classes from home due to the following reasons.

First of all,some students when offered distance learning will not pay attention to their lessons. They will distracted either by their cell phones or electronic devices. And we all know students always like to be on their cell phones at anytime and anywhere. Also,Students can be distracted either by their parents or siblings which may cause them lack behind ahead of their lessons. So when all of this happens , students may be delayed which will cause them to fail and waste of time. For example,my cousin came to the United States of America with his siblings and he was permitted to to take one of his subjects or courses online. And anytime he gets home,he doesnt get a peace of mind because of the disturbances and worries from his siblings. Due to this,he fell apart in his studies which caused him to fail the course.

Another reason is that,some students finds it difficult and boring to learn on their own pace. Because they encounter a lot of problems in their studies. Students finds it very hard to understand lessons without the presence and explanation of a teacher. And again,students finds it very boring when learning on their own because there is no form of oral conversation between the teacher and student. Some students prefer being active in studies rather being dull or inactive. So when all these happens,the students may skip the contents because he or she doesn't get any understanding,

or close the contents and go to sleep. For instance,I had a friend who was struggling with these same problems,he feels bored and difficult to understand in distance learning. So anytime he gets to sit for the lessons,he feels sleepy during a short period of time. He sometimes drink a whole cup of thick coffee but it doesn't make any changes. So what he does is to off the computer and go to bed. And this hinders his academic performance each year.

Lastly,students feel fatigue or weak in distance learning since they don't get time to take rest after school. Some students even have to close work after school before taking the online class. With these,it makes student lazy and sleepy when he or she sits in fronts of the computer to learn. And me myself is experiencing this problem. When school closes, I have to walk half a mile before I gets home,and from there,I work on my assignments and take my shower. So by the time I will be done,then it is getting late, and I still have to take this classes online. I feel tired in learning at times which retards my level of learning.

From these reasons, I would like to conclude that,students would not benefit from distance learning because there are so many disadvantages from it which has brought low level academics in their studies.

Thank you.

Although allowing students to attend classes from home through online platforms or video conferencing seems like a convenient option, I believe that students do not actually benefit from distance learning. There are several key reasons why studying from home is ineffective for most learners.

First of all, many students struggle to pay attention during online lessons because of the many distractions at home. It is very easy for them to get distracted by their smartphones or other electronic devices, especially since young people love using their phones constantly. Additionally, family members like parents and siblings can interrupt their study time, making it hard to focus. When students cannot concentrate, they fall behind and eventually fail their courses. For instance, my cousin, who moved to the United States, was allowed to take one of his classes online. However, whenever he was at home, his siblings constantly disturbed him, and he could not find a quiet place to study. Consequently, his grades dropped, and he ended up failing the class.

Another major issue is that many students find it difficult and boring to study at their own pace. Without a teacher physically present to explain the material, understanding complex topics becomes a real challenge. Furthermore, online learning lacks the active, face-to-face communication between teachers and students that keeps lessons interesting. Without this interaction, students often become disengaged, skip difficult parts of the lesson, or simply fall asleep. For example, I have a friend who faced this exact problem. He found online classes so boring and hard to follow that he would feel sleepy almost immediately after starting. Even drinking a large cup of strong coffee did not help him stay awake. In the end, he would just turn off his computer and go to sleep, which seriously damaged his academic performance over the school year.

Lastly, distance learning often causes extreme fatigue because students do not get enough time to rest. Many students have busy schedules, and some even have to go to work before they can log into their online classes. This busy routine makes them feel exhausted and lazy when they finally sit in front of the computer. I have experienced this problem myself. After my regular school day ends, I have to walk half a mile to get home. Once I arrive, I must finish my homework and take a shower. By the time I am done, it is already late, but I still have to attend my online classes. Because I am so tired, it is very difficult to absorb the information, which slows down my learning progress.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that students do not benefit from distance learning. The constant distractions at home, the lack of direct teacher interaction, and the physical exhaustion it causes all contribute to lower academic performance. Therefore, traditional classroom learning remains a much better option for students.

In my opinion, students should be allowed to design their own summer projects. This approach is beneficial because it allows students to produce highly creative work, enjoy the process much more, and experience far less stress during their summer break.

When students have the freedom to explore their interests without a rigid checklist, they can produce amazing work. They can also have fun collaborating on these projects with their friends.

Finally, designing their own projects helps reduce academic pressure. Instead of worrying about getting a perfect grade or meeting strict guidelines, students can work at their own pace. They can even design their own checklists and share them with classmates, turning the project into a fun activity rather than a stressful chore.

In conclusion, allowing students to plan their own summer projects is a great idea because it boosts creativity, makes learning fun, and reduces stress.

I support the idea of starting an afterschool homework club. Many students struggle to complete their assignments on their own, so having teachers available to assist them would be a great way to reduce failing grades. Of course, there are some potential problems. For instance, some students might try to copy answers from others and leave early. To prevent this, the club should not allow students to look at each other's work until they have finished their own tasks. Other students might treat the club as a social hour and talk the entire time. Nevertheless, there will always be responsible students who focus on their work, avoid distractions, and do what is expected of them.

This program can help students develop better study habits and achieve higher grades. Since the students who join are usually those who care about their education, they are likely to behave well. Ultimately, this club gives struggling students a valuable opportunity to improve their academic performance and prepare for a successful next school year.

People often debate whether it is better to work individually or in a team. While some prefer the independence of working alone, others enjoy collaborating with a group. In my opinion, working in groups is the most effective way to progress because it allows us to acquire more knowledge and gain a deeper understanding of the task at hand.

To begin with, collaborating with others enhances our performance at school or work by exposing us to new ideas. For instance, in my English class, the teacher once divided us into groups of four to answer several questions on the board. When we shared our answers with the rest of the class, we realized that every group had unique viewpoints. This experience taught us all something new. As the saying goes, we learn something new every day.

Furthermore, group work improves our comprehension because we can easily ask our teammates for assistance when we are confused. For example, during a history class, our teacher gave us an assignment to complete before the end of the period. I did not fully understand the instructions, so I asked one of my group members to explain them to me. Thanks to their help, I understood the task, shared my ideas, and contributed to the group. Indeed, we can achieve much more when we support one another.

On the other hand, many people believe that working alone is superior because it allows for better concentration. They argue that individual work prevents distractions and helps them finish tasks faster. A friend of mine, for instance, always prefers to work by herself because she feels that group members often chat, distract each other, and accomplish very little. However, this argument is weak because if you work alone and do not understand something, you have no one to explain it to you. Getting stuck without any support can make it very difficult to complete the work.

In conclusion, working in a group offers numerous advantages, such as making new friends, understanding others better, and learning more about oneself. Collaborative work also reduces the pressure of meeting deadlines or feeling lost. Although some people prefer to work alone, I strongly believe that teamwork is far more beneficial. Ultimately, we all need a little help from others to truly improve.

Homework is often challenging, and students frequently need assistance to complete it. While an afterschool homework club sounds like a fun and helpful idea for students who struggle or need extra support, it is not a practical solution for everyone. Many students simply do not have free time after the school day ends.

An afterschool homework club would be difficult for a large number of students. Many people have busy schedules filled with extracurricular activities like sports practice, dance, music lessons, or other hobbies. Because of these commitments, they do not have enough time to attend a club, and they even struggle to finish their homework once they finally get home. This kind of club only benefits students who have no other afternoon activities and can easily stay late.

Personally, I am against having an afterschool homework club. I often have sports practice after school, which leaves me with very little time, though I always try my best to complete my assignments for the next day. Furthermore, we must consider the teachers. They also have busy lives outside of school, such as taking care of their children or feeding their pets, so they might not be able to stay late to supervise a club.

Another major issue is transportation. Many parents work late or are unavailable, meaning many students would not have a ride home after the club ends. It is also unlikely that the school would provide food, leaving students hungry during these extra hours. Instead of an afterschool club, a better solution would be to schedule a homework period during the very last class of the school day.

Having this study block at the end of the day would solve many problems. Students with busy afternoon schedules would not have to worry about finishing their homework late at night. It would also give everyone a much-needed break after a long day of learning. Additionally, teachers could benefit from this time by grading papers or preparing lessons while the students work quietly.

Alternatively, the school could place this homework block at the beginning of the day. This would allow students who did not finish their work the night before to complete it before classes start. However, my favorite option is still the last-period study block. It gives both students and teachers a break, ensures everyone finishes their assignments, and leaves the afternoon completely free for other activities.

Throughout the world, learning is a constant part of life. We are always discovering new things about people, animals, and the world around us. Anyone who is eager to learn every day is likely to succeed. While some people agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s claim that we can only grow by attempting things beyond what we have already mastered, I disagree. In my opinion, trying to do things that are completely beyond our current abilities will not lead to growth because we lack the necessary knowledge and experience to succeed.

To begin with, everyone wants to achieve something in life and find their ideal career. Those who are willing to learn and take part in new activities are more likely to reach their goals. Making an effort is the key to solving our problems. For example, my nineteen-year-old friend has been working as a restaurant server since she was seventeen. She knows the menu perfectly and understands how to restock everything. However, she is getting tired of this job but is hesitant to try anything else. Having only one work experience is not enough to understand other fields. If she does not make the effort to apply for a different job, she will never build the confidence needed to grow. Trying different jobs is essential because it opens up new opportunities.

Furthermore, having basic knowledge is crucial when attempting something new. People need a foundation of information before they can advance in their careers. For instance, when I was in the eighth grade, my teacher used to sit with me during lunch, and we would talk about various topics. As middle school was ending, I asked her for advice about entering high school. She warned me that high school would be much more challenging and that I needed to take my education seriously. She explained that I would need to pass exams, maintain a high GPA, and start planning my future career. Her guidance helped prepare me. This shows that acquiring knowledge beforehand is what truly allows a person to develop.

Clearly, jumping into tasks that are far beyond our mastery without preparation does not lead to growth. A complete lack of experience often makes people retreat into their comfort zones, while a lack of knowledge leaves them feeling lost. Some might argue that we must attempt things we haven't mastered to grow, asking how anyone can develop by just repeating daily routines. However, you cannot learn something new without some basic understanding. For example, when my father moved to the United States at age fourteen, he spoke very little English and could only write a few words. Instead of jumping into complex tasks, he put all his effort into learning the language step-by-step. By achieving small goals, he gradually overcame his limitations and eventually reached the level he wanted.

In conclusion, both experience and knowledge are necessary for true personal growth. Imagine working on a science project about a mysterious animal that changes its size, color, and shape. To truly understand it, you would want to study its behavior and lifestyle deeply, rather than just looking at basic facts. Similarly, we must build a strong foundation of knowledge and experience before we can successfully take on greater challenges and grow.

What are the benefits of pairing older and younger students together? Creating these partnerships can have a highly positive impact on students. This is because younger students can discover new ways of studying, receive valuable advice about what to expect in high school, and learn effective techniques for managing stress.

To begin with, pairing these two groups is beneficial because it allows them to share different learning methods. Older students can demonstrate their own study techniques to the younger ones. If a younger student is struggling with a homework assignment, they can ask questions, and their older partner can explain how to solve the problems using their own skills. Furthermore, older students can share useful shortcuts in various subjects. Having an older peer explain these different learning styles is incredibly helpful when younger students face difficult academic challenges.

Secondly, older students can offer valuable advice on what to expect in high school. They can explain the difficulty of the classes and how much homework to anticipate. Additionally, they can recommend fun elective courses, such as theater or cheerleading, while younger students can share what activities they are interested in trying. Older peers can also highlight the essential skills that are necessary for success. Being prepared for the transition to high school is crucial, and older students are perfect guides for this preparation.

Finally, older students can teach younger ones how to manage academic stress. They can share their personal test-taking strategies and offer tips on how to prepare for exams. For instance, they can explain how they study and how they organize their time and workspace to stay focused. Learning these stress-management techniques early on will make a significant difference when younger students eventually enter high school.

In conclusion, pairing younger and older students is an excellent idea. It allows younger students to learn new study methods, get a realistic preview of high school life, and discover useful ways to handle stress. Ultimately, bringing these two groups together provides a unique and highly beneficial experience for everyone involved.

Human beings rely heavily on technology to survive, and it is almost impossible to imagine our lives without it. From the moment we open our eyes in the morning until we fall asleep at night, technology is a constant part of our daily routines. Over the years, it has developed rapidly, especially when we compare the very first telephones to the smart devices we use today. Although some people worry about its negative effects, such as young children becoming addicted to screens and crying when they are taken away, the overall benefits of technology are incredibly significant and far outweigh the drawbacks.

The journey of modern communication technology began with Alexander Graham Bell’s invention of the telephone. His original device was extremely different from today's mobile phones; it was large, heavy, and shaped like a brick. Because it was designed only for home use and could not be carried around easily, it was not considered an immediate necessity by a society that was used to living without it. However, as time went on, other inventors built upon Bell's ideas, reducing the size and weight of the phone while increasing its features. Originally, phones were only used for long-distance voice calls so people could talk without being face-to-face. Eventually, competition grew, and many different companies started producing electronic devices. In the early 2000s, Apple introduced the first iPhone, which quickly became a global sensation. Today, Apple and other companies produce a wide variety of daily products, including tablets, smartwatches, laptops, wireless headphones, and portable chargers, which have become essential parts of our lives.

While these technological developments have raised concerns about screen addiction in young children, technology can actually be very beneficial for early development. Parents have the responsibility to manage this by setting strict limits on screen time and monitoring what their children watch. When used correctly, technology can help toddlers learn basic skills like shapes, colors, and communication before they even start school, giving them a helpful head start. Educational platforms, such as ABCmouse, offer interactive and enjoyable ways for young children to study and develop their minds through fun activities.

Today, technology is integrated into almost every aspect of our lives, both inside and outside our homes. Indoors, we rely on devices like security cameras, thermostats, air conditioning, refrigerators, Wi-Fi routers, and smart TVs to stay comfortable and safe. Outside, we depend on cars, traffic signals, and GPS systems to travel to our destinations efficiently. Furthermore, if we need to research a topic for school or work, we no longer have to wait for a library to open; we can access unlimited information instantly from any location with a simple swipe on our smartphones or computers. Most importantly, technology plays a vital role in healthcare. In hospitals, advanced medical machinery saves lives daily, from helping newborn babies to treating seriously injured patients. Scientists also use technology to research cures for dangerous diseases and find ways to prevent them in the future.

In conclusion, the creation of technology has greatly improved human life in almost every way. Without these innovations, we would face far more accidents and preventable deaths. As technology continues to advance, it will make us even better prepared to handle future global challenges and tragedies. Ultimately, technology has been an incredibly positive force that benefits billions of people around the world every single day.

The famous British Prime Minister Winston Churchill once noted that success is the ability to move from one failure to another without losing your enthusiasm. I completely agree with this perspective. Failure plays an essential role in achieving our goals. It is not just a negative outcome; rather, it is about understanding our errors, gaining valuable experience, and refusing to give up. By analyzing what went wrong, we can create a better plan to achieve even greater results than we originally anticipated. This is why failure is a fundamental part of the journey toward success.

One of the clearest ways failure helps us succeed is by teaching us important lessons. Throughout history, humanity has repeatedly progressed by learning from past mistakes. A great historical example of this is the League of Nations. Established after the First World War to maintain global peace, this organization ultimately failed to prevent further conflict. However, instead of giving up on international cooperation, global leaders learned from these structural weaknesses and created the United Nations. Today, the UN remains one of the most successful international organizations in history, demonstrating how a major failure can pave the way for a lasting triumph.

In addition to learning lessons, perseverance is another crucial element of success. Giving up should never be an option when facing obstacles. The legendary soccer player Pelé is a perfect example of this determination. From a very young age, people told him he would never make it as a professional athlete because he lacked sufficient talent. Despite this criticism, he kept working hard and proved his doubters wrong. Later, during his first World Cup, he suffered a severe knee injury during training. Doctors warned him that he would not be able to play in the tournament. However, Pelé refused to give up. He did his rehabilitation exercises daily and eventually got the chance to play in the later stages of the tournament, helping his team win. His story shows how mental strength and resilience can turn setbacks into historic achievements.

Another vital aspect of the relationship between failure and success is the willingness to try again. Once you have analyzed your mistakes, you are better prepared to make another attempt. Space exploration perfectly illustrates this concept. In the early days of space travel, many rockets failed, with several exploding due to technical errors. However, scientists did not abandon their goals. They carefully studied each disaster to understand what went wrong, which allowed them to improve their technology. Consequently, humans successfully launched satellites, sent astronauts into orbit, and now explore distant parts of our galaxy. This progress was only possible because we used our failures as stepping stones to try again.

Of course, some people argue that failure has no connection to success. They claim that it is possible to succeed on the very first attempt, that mistakes do not teach us anything useful, and that repeated failures destroy a person's motivation. However, I believe these arguments are incorrect. Achieving success on the first try is extremely rare, and we almost always gain valuable insights from our errors. Furthermore, losing enthusiasm is a personal choice. We have the power to control our own attitude and keep our spirits high despite setbacks. Failure is an inevitable part of life, but it is also a powerful tool for personal and societal growth.

In conclusion, failure and success are deeply connected. Failing is not a disaster; it is an opportunity to learn, gain experience, and identify our weaknesses. The most important factor is our attitude, as we are the ones who decide whether to maintain our enthusiasm or give up. Winston Churchill’s words remain highly relevant today. By accepting our mistakes, planning our next steps carefully, and trying again with passion, we can turn our past failures into future victories that exceed our original expectations.

School should be a comfortable place for everyone, but different types of schools offer different experiences. Studying from home has both advantages and disadvantages. One major benefit of homeschooling is that you can focus on your work without being distracted by classmates. In traditional schools, some students do not care about their education, which can distract others and cause them to fail or repeat a grade. If you have to retake a class at home, you can do it privately without feeling judged. In contrast, repeating a year in a regular school can be a very embarrassing experience.

Another advantage of learning from home is receiving one-on-one attention. In traditional schools, classrooms are often crowded, making it difficult for teachers to help every single student. On the other hand, some students are forced to study at home due to physical disabilities or because they are famous and need privacy. These students might actually prefer going to a regular school because staying at home all the time can make them feel trapped and lonely. After all, socializing with peers is very important for a person's well-being.

Furthermore, homeschooling often allows students to finish their courses much faster. However, it also comes with extra costs. Public schools usually provide free education and free lunches. In contrast, homeschooling can be quite expensive because families have to pay for their own food, computers, and internet connection. Despite these high expenses, investing in a home education is worth it because it still leads to valuable knowledge and qualifications for your future career.

In conclusion, getting an education from home is a great way to earn a diploma and prepare for the future. Ultimately, whether you choose to attend a public school, a private school, or study from home, any form of education will benefit you in many different ways throughout your life.

A year ago, I believed that business was the perfect career path for me, but it turned out to be incredibly difficult. I struggled in my classes, failed, and felt extremely stressed because I did not know what to do. Although I realized business was not my passion, I worried it was too late to change my mind. Fortunately, after speaking with my academic counselor, I learned I could switch majors. Now, I have chosen a different path that feels right, though I still worry I might change my mind again since I can be quite indecisive. However, I have realized this is completely normal after talking to my classmates, who experienced the exact same feelings. While some people argue that committing to a career at a young age is beneficial because it allows students to take relevant high school courses, I believe it is actually a bad idea. Choosing a career too early often leads to picking the wrong path and ignores the fact that young people are naturally undecided about their futures.

Supporters of early career commitment argue that it helps students select high school classes that prepare them for their future jobs. However, they fail to see how this can become a burden. I frequently hear my friends and classmates complain about how difficult and miserable their classes are, yet they refuse to drop them because they believe these courses are necessary for their future careers. This pressure only makes students feel unhappy and highly stressed. The best solution is to allow students to change their minds. If a chosen path is not working out, or if they simply picked it because they were unsure, they should have the freedom to try something else.

There are several reasons why early commitment is a mistake, but two main points stand out. First, young people are highly likely to choose a career that is completely wrong for them. Many children grow up wanting to be just like their parents, aiming to study the same subjects or attend the same universities. In other cases, parents put intense pressure on their children to pursue specific, high-status jobs. Consequently, students often choose paths based on their parents' wishes rather than their own interests. When they eventually realize they do not enjoy the subject, they become stressed, unhappy, and may even want to drop out of school entirely. If we were to survey students about their choices, I am certain an overwhelming majority would admit they chose the wrong career path at some point.

Second, committing early is unrealistic because young people are naturally undecided. With so many career options available, it is extremely difficult to choose just one. As students grow, they often discover new skills and interests that lead them toward different fields, even if they were previously good at their first choice. Making wrong decisions and trying out new things is a fundamental part of life and learning. When students make a mistake in their career choice, it teaches them valuable lessons. Some might even decide to study multiple subjects or take a variety of classes to reach their goals. Being undecided and experimenting with different courses is actually beneficial because it helps students discover what they truly want.

In conclusion, forcing students to commit to a career at a young age is a bad idea because they are likely to choose the wrong path and are often too undecided to make such a permanent choice. Young people can be impulsive and make quick decisions without understanding what a career actually involves. Instead of forcing early decisions, we should support students in exploring different options so they can figure out what they genuinely want to learn. This approach will ultimately help them make much better decisions for their future.

Furthermore, when people make multiple mistakes, they often feel overwhelmed and make even more errors while trying to solve them all at once. I experienced this during an exam when I tried to answer several difficult questions at the same time, which only confused me and ruined my performance.

In conclusion, I disagree with the idea that problems are opportunities to do our best. Not everyone knows how to recover from a mistake, and many problems cause lasting damage that cannot be repaired. Ultimately, the best way to achieve greatness is to avoid making mistakes in the first place.

He came from a poor family, and walked a long distance to his school everyday. When he started running, he was not good at all. He worked day and night to get to where he is. Success is a dream for most and a reality for only a few. When it comes to how success is achieved, it creates a great question in all our minds and that is,"How can I be successful?". Some say that success is achieved by going through failures without giving up or without losing hope. That is a truly arguable idea and some might think different. But I fully agree with that idea.

The fact that almost all of the masterminds that are known for their creations of the bulb, physics theories, telephone and many more of the things we take for granted at the moment told the story of how they tried and failed many times than they count. And that is one proof of the point that success doesn't come without failure.

There might be some people that argue this point by pointing out that many people have tried and failed and tried again but it didn't help them achieve their dreams. That is a good point but the fact is that failing is not the only thing that determines your success, but failing and not being discouraged is what really counts. If we plan to achieve a goal, we shouldn't lose our excitement for that specific thing we're doing, we should rather be more encouraged to try harder and to find another way to make it work.

For example, when we first built a rocket,it wasn't done in a day or in the first try. Engineers tried to fix the problem in the mechanical part. Scientists tried to see if their calculations was wrong or if the combination of the chemicals didn't work and many others tried to fix it but they failed more than a couple of times. By not giving up though, it was a success at last.

It might not always seem like it but failure leads to success. The main point is not giving up and not losing our enthusiasm. As the saying goes, "If you fail once, try and try harder". Never give up on your dreams and don't be discouraged by failure.

This is because working in a team allows them to share the workload, exchange ideas, and support one another, making the process much more efficient. Personally, I believe that group work is highly beneficial for students and is the better choice.

First of all, students often face a heavy workload with multiple projects each term, especially major assignments that count for ten percent of their final grade. When working in a group, this heavy burden can be divided among the members. Furthermore, every student has unique strengths. A task that is difficult for one person might be easy for another, allowing the team to utilize everyone's individual talents to achieve a better result.

Secondly, group projects teach students the value of cooperation, which is an essential skill for their future careers. In the professional world, companies frequently assign projects to teams rather than individuals because combining different areas of expertise increases productivity. Businesses often emphasize the phrase "work as a team" to boost efficiency. By assigning group work, teachers help students gain this valuable teamwork experience and learn from their peers.

Additionally, collaborating with classmates helps students build confidence. They can discuss different topics together and find the best solutions. For students who cannot meet at someone's house, schools usually provide after-school spaces to work together. Group work also supports students who struggle with deadlines, as team members can motivate and assist them to ensure the work is completed on time.

In conclusion, students should not have to tackle large, time-consuming projects all by themselves. Since modern companies rely on teamwork to increase efficiency, teachers should adopt the same approach. Allowing group work in the classroom helps students improve their grades, submit their assignments on time, develop cooperation skills, and benefit from diverse perspectives to produce the best possible results.

Winston Churchill’s famous words hold great meaning for many people today. While some individuals manage to stand up again after failing and continue chasing their dreams, others feel discouraged and decide to quit. It is essential to look at both of these reactions, as Churchill's message reminds us of the vital importance of perseverance.

To begin with, we should never give up because failure is a valuable opportunity to learn from our mistakes. When we fail at something, we must realize that it is not the end of the world. Making a mistake simply teaches us how to improve and get it right the next time. Believing in our ability to achieve our goals is crucial, and standing up for what we believe in will always lead us in the right direction.

Another key reason to keep going is the desire to reach our highest ambitions. If we truly want to achieve something, we have to work hard for it. Many people who fail believe they have only wasted their time, and they choose to stop trying. However, we cannot always win in life, and experiencing failure is a natural part of human existence. Even though failing feels disappointing, pushing through these difficult moments is what allows us to feel proud of ourselves and achieve true success.

On the other hand, those who choose to give up are the ones who truly fail. People who expect to get a great job, enter a prestigious school, or reach their dreams without making any mistakes are usually the first to quit when things go wrong. In contrast, successful individuals only achieved their goals because they worked hard and refused to quit during tough times. When people fail, they often put themselves down and claim they are not smart enough, but everyone faces struggles. During these difficult times, it is important to remember that we can rely on our friends and family to support us and help us solve our problems.

In conclusion, when we set a goal for ourselves, we must never quit halfway through. By working hard, we can eventually reach whatever we set our minds to. When we face obstacles, the support of the people who care about us can help us get back on track. Ultimately, by refusing to give up, we can build our self-confidence and face life with greater courage.

Is a four-day school week with ten-hour days a good idea? In my opinion, this change does not make sense. If we adopt this schedule, working students will lose valuable work hours, others will waste their extra day off doing nothing at home, and young people will spend more time using electronic devices instead of studying. Therefore, we should stick to the traditional schedule.

Many students have part-time jobs after school and need time to travel home and prepare for their shifts. If the school day becomes much longer, working will become almost impossible because they will only be able to work a few hours a day. Many students, especially seniors, need this income to pay their bills or save for college. For this reason, it is much better to maintain the standard five-day week with six-hour school days.

School administrators might assume that students will use their extra day off to study at home. However, they forget that many students need academic support or prefer studying in a school environment. With one less school day and longer hours, more students might fail their exams and projects. For instance, those who usually study in the school library after class will not be able to do so because it will be too late when school ends. We should keep the current schedule to help these students succeed.

Although some people believe that cutting a school day will save money and electricity, they do not realize that students will simply stay home and use energy there. At home, they will spend hours watching television, playing video games, and using their phones. In contrast, when students are at school, their use of electronic devices is limited to lunch and breaks. Consequently, staying at school actually reduces overall energy consumption compared to spending a whole day at home.

In conclusion, it is much better for students to keep the traditional five-day schedule. This ensures that they do not lose working hours, have enough time and resources to study at school, and do not spend excessive time on electronic devices. While saving energy and money is a positive goal, the reality is that students will not practice energy conservation at home. Therefore, maintaining the regular school week is the best choice for everyone.

Choosing a career is one of the most significant decisions in a person's life. With thousands of options available, a person's job often reflects their personality and interests. Because career choices are so important, many people spend a lot of time thinking about them. Deciding on a career path at an early age is highly beneficial for students. By committing early, young people can understand what a job actually involves, discover an enjoyable daily activity, and avoid future stress in their adult lives.

First of all, starting early allows students to gain a realistic understanding of their chosen profession. For instance, many students want to become doctors but do not actually know what the job entails or how to treat patients. To truly understand this field, they need hands-on experience. By actively exploring a career early on, students can gather valuable information. Furthermore, they can easily research any profession they are interested in, such as dentistry, to find out what qualifications are required. Engaging with a career path early gives students the time and resources they need to prepare for their future.

Secondly, focusing on a career path helps students find productive and enjoyable activities for their free time. Many teenagers do not have constructive hobbies and often feel bored after school. Instead of wasting their free time, these students can participate in after-school programs that teach them about different professions. Getting involved in career-related activities can actually become a fun hobby. It allows young people to discover what they are truly passionate about, keeping them engaged and happy. Ultimately, starting early helps them find something that is truly meaningful to them.

Finally, committing to a career early prepares students for adulthood and reduces future anxiety. Many young people reach adulthood without knowing what they want to do, which makes finding a job very difficult. However, if students spend time during their school years reading and learning about a specific field, they will not face this struggle. They will easily transition into their chosen path. High school graduation is often a stressful time because of the pressure to find a job, but students who already know their interests will feel much more confident and relaxed. For those who are completely unsure of their future, spending time researching and joining career programs is the best way to get ideas and reduce anxiety.

Some people argue that young students should not commit to a career because they do not know enough about the working world yet. However, avoiding the decision only leads to employment difficulties later in life. The best way for students to learn about jobs is to participate in career fairs and gain early experience, which will lead to future success. In conclusion, committing to a career at an early age is highly advantageous. It helps students become well-educated about their options, provides them with a fulfilling hobby, and ensures a stress-free transition into the job market.

I agree that seeking guidance from experts to make wise decisions can have a great impact on our lives. Experts and authorities can provide us with advice to make good decisions in life and accomplish our goals more easily.

Influence can be expressed in three main ways: through words, actions, and motivation. While some people argue that leading by example is the only way to influence others, this is not the case. By looking at how words, actions, and motivation function, it becomes clear that setting an example is just one of several ways to inspire and guide people.

First of all, spoken words can have a powerful impact. Many people are highly receptive to verbal advice from influential figures. For instance, a YouTuber named Alpha M helps men become more successful. If he lacked his charismatic speaking style, his audience would probably ignore his advice. This shows that communication is not just helpful, but absolutely essential for guiding others, provided the speaker knows what they are talking about.

In addition, actions are a crucial way to demonstrate influence without using words. Actions show people how to behave and what to achieve. A great example of this is Lionel Messi, the famous soccer player who has played since childhood. His incredible skills on the field have inspired countless people to improve both in sports and in their personal lives. Without his active talent, his impact would be much weaker. Therefore, actions are vital, though motivation also plays a major role.

Motivation is another key element of influence because it reflects a person's character, responsibility, and success—qualities that people admire today. For example, a police officer named Generic_Name has shown great dedication in his career. His strong motivation has earned him several awards and inspired citizens to respect the law and contribute to society. If he lacked this drive, his ability to encourage lawful behavior would be lost. Clearly, motivation can inspire millions of people.

Despite these points, some argue that setting a physical example is the only effective way to influence society. However, relying solely on an example is often insufficient. For instance, a teacher at Generic_school might lead by example by never using his phone in class, yet his students might still use theirs. If the teacher combined his example with persuasive words and genuine motivation, the students would be much more likely to follow his rules. Thus, setting an example is only a small part of the bigger picture.

In conclusion, leading by example is certainly not the only path to influencing others. True influence is a combination of words, actions, and motivation. Words can guide people verbally, actions show them how to succeed practically, and motivation inspires them to do better. Rather than relying on a single method, using all three of these qualities is the most effective way to make a lasting impact on society.

We achieve much more in life when we are active and constantly taking action. By pushing ourselves beyond our comfort zones, we ensure continuous personal growth. Every action we take, no matter how small, brings some form of return or reward. When we set a goal and work hard to achieve it, we build self-confidence, knowing that our efforts can produce real results. This success then motivates us to keep striving. While some people believe they can get results by doing nothing, the truth is that real accomplishment requires dedication, hard work, and active effort. If we do not take action, we cannot expect to achieve anything meaningful in life.

Taking action is essential for personal growth because pushing ourselves allows us to develop. I remember a clear example of this from when I was in the sixth grade. My school organized an annual math competition, and only the fastest math students were selected to participate. The teacher offered after-school review sessions to help us prepare, but I could not attend them because I had swimming practice at the same time, which my parents had already paid for. I felt very sad, but I realized that if I truly wanted to be in that competition, I had to find another way. I decided to wake up two hours earlier every morning to practice math, and I also spent my lunch breaks working on math problems in the library. This sacrifice paid off when my teacher announced the list of participants, and my name was on it. My mother always told me that failing is just a part of learning; the next time you try, you will not make the same mistakes. Ultimately, through hard work and determination, you can achieve any goal in life. This is a lesson I will carry with me forever.

Furthermore, we gain a lot by doing things for others, because every action we take brings some kind of reward. When we patiently and willingly help others without expecting anything in return, we experience a deep sense of personal satisfaction. For instance, seeing a hungry child on the street and offering them food brings joy to both the child and ourselves. I experienced this feeling of connection when I went to work with my mother one day. We were cleaning the house of an elderly woman who lived alone with her dog. I asked my mother if I could visit her on weekends to keep her company. Over time, this sweet and kind woman became incredibly special to me, and she even called me her granddaughter. Eventually, her son came to take her to live with him in another city. Saying goodbye was incredibly difficult, but before she left, she told me that I would always be in her heart and that she would cherish the happy times we spent together. That experience taught me that when you do something kind for someone else, the emotional reward can change your life forever.

Active effort also builds the self-confidence we need to face life's challenges. When we work hard to achieve our goals, we prove to ourselves that we can overcome obstacles. For example, when you have a mountain of school assignments, pushing yourself to complete them builds the confidence that you can accomplish anything you set your mind to. This self-belief is crucial when making major life decisions. I saw this in my sister when she was deciding on her college major. She was terrified of choosing a difficult career path because she was afraid of failing. However, she found the confidence to believe in herself and took the challenge anyway. Watching her move forward despite her fear made me admire her deeply. We must banish the fear of failure from our lives and replace it with the confidence to believe in our own potential.

Taking action and working toward our goals is always better than sitting back and expecting success to happen on its own.

In conclusion, by actively doing things, we grow as individuals, bring happiness to others, and build the self-confidence needed to face any challenge. It is vital to understand that while we all have the opportunity to improve our lives and reach our goals, these achievements do not happen by accident. They require hard work, dedication, and a strong belief in ourselves.

Without these face-to-face support systems, students are likely to struggle, and their grades will suffer.

In-person school is often seen as a second home where students inspire each other and build deep friendships. It also provides a network of teachers and counselors who can offer personal advice. When stuck at home, students often feel lonely and bored. This isolation can worsen mental health issues like stress, anxiety, and depression, which are common among teenagers today. Going to school serves as a healthy distraction from personal problems and gives students access to professional support.

Finally, online classes are particularly challenging for students who struggle with self-discipline. At home, there is no teacher physically present to keep them focused, make sure they stay awake, or remind them to complete their homework. Additionally, virtual learning makes group work difficult. Working in teams is a great way for students to learn from each other, stay motivated, and have fun. Many people view technology as an extension of our own bodies. For instance, we carry our smartphones everywhere we go. Although we rely on technology daily, it often leads to distractions and reduces our face-to-face contact with others. Even though some argue that technology improves our lives, it actually has a mostly negative impact.

Of course, technology does bring several benefits to our daily routines. In the workplace, digital tools make our jobs much easier and help us work more efficiently. When it comes to communication, mobile phones allow us to stay in touch with loved ones, check on their well-being, and coordinate plans. Furthermore, technology plays a vital role in education. Devices like computers and smartphones assist students with their daily homework and research, while also providing teachers with useful resources for their lessons.

However, technology is also a major source of distraction. In schools, students frequently use their phones, which diverts their attention away from lessons and classmates. This unauthorized device use often results in falling grades and a loss of interest in education, turning a simple tool into an addiction. Beyond the classroom, using phones while driving is extremely dangerous. Whether texting, changing music, or looking down at a GPS map, these actions take a driver's eyes off the road, which can easily lead to serious car accidents. This clearly demonstrates how devices make us lose focus on our immediate surroundings.

Additionally, technology reduces real-life interaction with other people. It is common to see children and teenagers walking around with their heads down, staring at their screens. As a result, young people are communicating less with their parents, relatives, and peers. This lack of face-to-face contact damages their social skills, making them feel awkward when trying to approach or talk to someone in person. It is disheartening to see how technology is weakening our ability to connect, effectively isolating us from the real world.

In conclusion, while technology offers undeniable advantages, its overall influence on our lives is negative. Since technology is now deeply integrated into our society, we cannot simply get rid of it. However, it continues to distract us and damage our personal relationships. Ultimately, technology itself is not the enemy; rather, the problem lies in our addictive habits and how we choose to use it. If we could limit our screen time to when it is truly necessary, the world would be a much better place.

School is a very important part in a person's life, however it takes away most of student's and teacher's day. In a normal public middle school in Maryland, a student first class starts at 8:15 in the morning and the last class ends at 3:00 pm. Which means that a student spends 7 hours and 25 minutes in school, that is a long time for a person to be receiving information nonstop. The school board should not extend the school day, because that would take time away from activities that students need or will need in the future, such as: students would have less time to do homework or study, students would have less time to participate in after school activities like sports, and students wouldl have less time to volunteer in community events.

Students would have less time to do homework or study. Students already spends more than seven hours at school and usually has 6-8 classes that last 45 minutes each from those 6-8 classes at least

3 would have assigned homework to the students which means that the students would need time to complete their homework with accuracy, if the school days werre extended students would have less time to complete their homework which means that their grade might go decrease for missing assignments.

Students would have less time to participate in after school activities such as sports, or clubs.

Every healthy person should exercise for at least 1 hour per day and at school not every student takes physical education (P.E.) as a course which leads to the thought that students might not me be getting the necessary amount of exercise per day, and even if a student did take P.E. a normal class lasts 45 minutes, which is not enough for a healthy person. If the school board were to add one and a half hours to the school day students would have less time to practice in an after school team. Clubs are just like sports are a very big thing in a school, clubs shows students opportunities they usually would not get in a school day. if the school board were to extend the school day students that are parts of clubs would probably get less time to spend time in those clubs.

Although school plays a vital role in a person's life, it already consumes a major part of a student's day. For instance, in a typical Maryland public middle school, classes run from 8:15 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. This means students spend nearly seven and a half hours at school, which is a very long time to absorb information without a break. Therefore, the school board should not lengthen the school day. Doing so would take away valuable time that students need for essential activities, such as doing homework, participating in extracurricular sports and clubs, and volunteering in the community.

First of all, a longer school day would leave students with less time to study and complete their homework. Currently, students attend six to eight 45-minute classes daily, and they usually receive homework from at least three of them. To complete these assignments accurately, they need sufficient time at home. If the school day were extended, students would have fewer hours in the evening to focus on their schoolwork. Consequently, their grades could easily drop because of incomplete or rushed assignments.

Secondly, extending the school day would reduce the time available for after-school activities like sports and clubs. Health experts recommend that everyone should get at least one hour of exercise daily. However, not all students take physical education, and even for those who do, a 45-minute gym class is simply not enough. If the school board added an hour and a half to the schedule, student-athletes would have much less time for team practices. Similarly, school clubs offer unique learning opportunities that students cannot get during regular classes. A longer school day would force these clubs to cut their meeting times short.

Finally, students would struggle to find time for community service. Volunteering is often a graduation requirement in many school districts. For example, students might need to complete 75 hours of community service by helping younger students or assisting teachers with classroom organization after school. These tasks usually take about two hours per session. If the school day were longer, students would have a harder time completing these required hours, which could ultimately prevent them from graduating.

In conclusion, it is much better for the school board to keep the school day at its current length. This ensures that students have enough time to balance their academic responsibilities with physical exercise, extracurricular clubs, and essential community service.

Understanding the difference between working for what we need and working for what we want ultimately helps us achieve both personal and social satisfaction.

A major debate in education today is whether schools should permit students to use smartphones for learning or ban them entirely from classrooms. While some teachers and staff argue that phones should be forbidden because they distract students, I strongly believe that allowing mobile phones for educational purposes is the right choice.

Using cell phones in class can actually improve academic performance. First, having a phone allows students to quickly look up information and take photos of the board, which is very helpful for studying at home. Second, if phones are banned, students often become anxious and spend the whole lesson waiting for the bell to ring instead of focusing on the teacher. For instance, I have a friend whose father confiscated her phone to force her to study. Instead of working harder, she rebelled, stopped studying completely, and ended up failing all her classes. This shows that banning phones can backfire, whereas allowing them supports the learning process.

Furthermore, mobile phones are essential for safety during emergencies. If there is a dangerous situation like a school lockdown, students can immediately call 911 for help. Similarly, during natural disasters such as fires or severe storms, having a phone allows students to contact their families to let them know they are safe. Additionally, when rules are too strict, students tend to break them. If phones are banned, students will just hide them and use them secretly, which is much riskier than using them openly under a teacher's supervision. Therefore, the benefits of having phones in class clearly outweigh the drawbacks.

In conclusion, although some people argue that cell phones have no place in the classroom, I strongly maintain that they should be allowed for educational use. Not only do they offer safety and prevent secret rule-breaking, but they are also much faster and more convenient to use than laptops. Ultimately, integrating phones into lessons is a highly effective way to support modern education.

Many schools now permit the use of mobile phones in classrooms for educational reasons. Allowing students to use their phones during class can have a very positive impact on their education, especially since young people use these devices constantly. Using phones can make students feel more motivated and comfortable while doing their schoolwork. Ultimately, this practice helps them complete their assignments, keep track of their grades, and improve their overall learning experience.

One major benefit of allowing cellphones in class is that it gives students the opportunity to complete their classwork and homework. Many students face heavy workloads and need extra time to finish everything. Additionally, personal problems can sometimes cause stress, making it hard to focus on schoolwork at home. For instance, some students have part-time jobs after school. After a long shift, extreme tiredness can make it nearly impossible to study at night. Based on these challenges, allowing students to use their phones for educational tasks in the classroom is a great way to help them manage their busy schedules.

Another reason to support this policy is that it allows students to monitor their grades and assignments. Some students miss school and do not know what homework they have, while others simply do not have time to check their portals at home. It is easy to forget about assignments after a busy day of chores and activities. By the time some students realize they have homework, it is already bedtime. Therefore, being able to check missed work during class lets students stay on track and immediately ask their teachers for assistance. For example, a student struggling with math can check their grades in class and get instant help from the teacher, which will ultimately improve their academic performance.

On the other hand, critics argue that cellphones are a major distraction because students might text or play games instead of paying attention. However, this view is incorrect because phones actually offer a more engaging and comfortable way to learn. When teachers incorporate technology, such as educational trivia games, students can learn while having fun. Furthermore, modern students are very good at remembering information they see on their screens. While older generations might worry that technology makes our brains lazy, it actually serves as a powerful tool that enhances the learning process.

In conclusion, permitting cellphones in the classroom has many advantages, such as helping students complete their work, monitor their progress, and learn more effectively. As the younger generation, we should use technology to expand our knowledge and prepare for the future. Making education more accessible and engaging is a choice we must make. Embracing these devices in school is simply a modern way to help students succeed both academically and in their future lives.

Almost everyone enjoys going to the beach or the pool, and I often think about what the most fun activity is. In my opinion, joining a swimming club is the best choice. Swimming is incredibly enjoyable because it helps me calm down when I am angry or upset, it gives me a chance to play and hang out with my friends, and it makes exercising feel much easier and more exciting.

To begin with, swimming is a wonderful activity because of its ability to soothe my mind when I am feeling down or angry. For instance, last year, right after school ended and everyone else had gone home, I dived into the pool and just started swimming. It brought me instant happiness. As I moved through the water, I loved hearing the sound of water splashing as my feet kicked, the gentle waves hitting the pool walls which made me feel relaxed, and the rush of water that made me feel so alive when I surfaced. Another time, during a two-day school trip to the beach, I felt really sad because our time there was ending. To cheer myself up, I changed my clothes, grabbed my camera, and went for a walk on the sand. Listening to the powerful sound of the crashing waves and the birds chirping while I took photos completely changed my mood. It turned into a peaceful and beautiful day, proving how calming swimming and being near the water can be.

Secondly, swimming is highly enjoyable because it is a social activity where you can hang out with friends and even make new ones. Although I do not mind swimming by myself, it is much more entertaining when others join. Once, I was swimming alone, but as soon as my friends arrived, we could not stop laughing. We spent the afternoon doing water tricks and racing against each other. At one point, two of my friends accidentally bumped heads underwater, and when they came up, we all burst into laughter. Furthermore, learning how to swim is much simpler when you have company. For example, a friend can support you when you are trying to learn how to float, which is much better than trying to figure it out alone. Even basic techniques like the dog paddle can be challenging for some, but practicing with friends makes the process fun rather than frustrating.

Finally, swimming is a great activity because it makes working out feel exciting rather than like a chore. I remember taking swimming lessons every Friday after school. Although I was reluctant at first, by the third session, I absolutely loved it. When I was ten years old, I weighed 145 pounds, but after starting these lessons, my weight dropped to 111 pounds. I realized that you do not notice physical improvements until you actually start enjoying the activity. Initially, I was only focused on losing weight and did not see any progress in my fitness or my swimming skills. However, once I stopped worrying and started having fun, I became more passionate and determined. Before I knew it, I was swimming much better and the weight just came off. When considering how to live our lives, is it better to make things up as we go or strictly follow a pre-written script? It is essential for everyone to develop their own individuality and stay true to themselves rather than trying to imitate others. By doing so, you discover who you really are, learn new ways to self-improve, and ultimately become a positive influence on those around you, helping them find their own direction. In the end, you must always trust your own path.

Discovering who you are means uncovering hidden aspects of your personality and abilities that you did not know existed. For instance, imagine you are in your spacious basement one day, playing your favorite music. As you listen to the rhythm, you start dancing with your usual moves. However, after a while, you lose yourself in the music and suddenly perform a backflip without any prior training. You are amazed because you had no idea you were capable of such a feat. From that moment on, you practice the move until it becomes natural. This is a perfect example of how stepping away from a script allows you to discover your true potential.

Furthermore, being true to yourself helps you recognize different ways to improve your life. This means making the necessary changes to become a better person. A clear example of this is the actor Robert Downey Jr., who once lived a chaotic life dominated by drug addiction and legal troubles. After making many poor decisions, he decided to turn his life around for his own sake and for the people who cared about him. It took him over five years of hard work, along with the support of his family and friends, to rebuild his life. Today, he is one of Hollywood's most successful actors, a dedicated family man, and an inspiration to millions. His journey shows how you can find your own way to self-improvement.

Some critics might argue that trying to be yourself is just a form of copying others. However, this is incorrect because you are actually taking advice and applying it through your own unique perspective. In this way, you write your own script while still appreciating the guidance you received. For example, suppose you want to talk to a girl at a party but have no idea how to approach her. You ask a friend for advice to avoid an awkward situation. He gives you some tips and demonstrates them, but right before you go over, he reminds you to just "be yourself." You take his advice but express it in your own style. The conversation goes incredibly well, she develops feelings for you, and you end up inspiring your other friends who face similar struggles. You followed a guide, but you executed it on your own terms.

In conclusion, staying true to yourself is vital because it proves that you do not need to copy anyone else to be someone of value. It allows you to understand yourself deeply, far more than you would understand a fictional character. It also helps you find new ways to grow, almost like leveling up in a video game. Finally, by being authentic, you become a positive role model for others. To live an authentic life, you should always listen to your intuition and do what feels right.

Many people believe that it is impossible to alter a first impression. This is because your behavior, the words you choose, and your overall appearance reveal who you truly are. Most people agree with this idea, as these three elements—actions, language, and looks—are things you can actively control and present to others.

To begin with, the way you behave when meeting someone for the first time is crucial. The old saying that actions speak louder than words is absolutely true. Once you act a certain way during an initial meeting, you cannot undo it. If you behave rudely or meanly toward someone you have just met, they will immediately assume you are not a pleasant person to be around. Therefore, it is vital to make a good start.

Furthermore, the language you use when speaking to a new acquaintance is highly important. You should avoid using inappropriate language, as this makes you seem disrespectful. Whether you use sophisticated vocabulary or just speak normally, speaking politely helps build trust over time. It is also helpful to try not to stutter too much, though most people will be understanding if you do. Additionally, it is best to avoid using too many hand gestures when you first meet someone.

In addition, your physical appearance plays a major role in first impressions. Although appearance reflects both your inner and outer self, people tend to focus heavily on how you look on the outside. When you present yourself poorly, others might assume you are a bad person and avoid socializing with you. Conversely, a neat and positive appearance makes people more open to being your friend, depending on their overall initial judgment of you.

Ultimately, if someone likes your behavior, speech, and appearance, they will likely want to become your friend. These initial judgments are incredibly powerful because they stay in people's minds and are extremely difficult to erase or modify.

On the other hand, it is sometimes possible to change someone's mind later on. Everyone has bad days, and some people are understanding enough to realize that a poor first meeting does not represent your true character. In these cases, you might be lucky enough to get a second chance to show who you really are.

In conclusion, many people agree that first impressions are permanent. Your actions, speech, and appearance are the key factors that shape how others see you. Since we interact with new people every day, we must always be mindful of how we act, speak, and look to ensure we leave a positive lasting memory.

Thomas Jefferson once suggested that we can achieve an incredible amount if we work without stopping. However, I believe that inactivity always serves an important purpose. To successfully complete our tasks, we must take regular breaks so that our bodies do not break down. While some people argue that we are more productive when we work constantly, rest remains essential.

First of all, taking breaks is necessary if we want to finish our work. This is the main reason why we have weekends off nowadays. Our bodies simply cannot function properly without a designated stopping point. Furthermore, without rest, the accumulated stress and pressure would make it impossible for us to sleep. Even animals need to rest after a long day of hard work so they can keep going.

Secondly, resting ensures that our bodies do not shut down while we are working. If we do not rest, we might easily fall asleep on the job, which can lead to dangerous situations. Depending on the type of work, exhaustion can cause serious workplace injuries. In the worst-case scenario, driving while tired can lead to fatal accidents, putting our own lives and the lives of others at risk.

On the other hand, some people believe that constant activity leads to greater achievements because tasks are completed much faster. They argue that we can learn new skills more quickly if we practice all day without stopping. Additionally, focusing solely on a task might produce better results. For instance, when building a house or an apartment, working without breaks would naturally shorten the construction time. It is like a continuous journey where you reach your destination faster by never stopping. For these people, constantly moving forward is the key to achieving goals.

In conclusion, inactivity serves a vital purpose because taking breaks helps us finish our work and prevents our bodies from collapsing. Although some people still believe that constant action is the best way to succeed, I believe it is ultimately up to each individual to decide whether or not to take time to rest.

I strongly agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s famous quote about individuality. It is wonderful to remain true to myself in a world that constantly tries to change me. Being myself gives me the freedom to do what I truly want, such as exploring beautiful natural places. I love the idea of visiting great forests and climbing high hills to experience the beauty of the earth.

Staying true to myself is especially important when the world pressures me to conform. For me, connecting with nature is a great way to maintain my individuality. Spending time outdoors and looking at different kinds of flowers and beautiful blossom trees is incredibly peaceful. These natural sights are very interesting to me and help me appreciate who I am.

Even though society tries to shape us into something else, going into a big forest helps me find my own path. While a forest might seem like just a collection of trees, looking closer reveals constantly changing life. Discovering new things, like fresh fruit growing on branches or beautiful bushes filled with flowers, makes the experience very exciting.

Sometimes, I feel like the world wants me to see and experience everything. This makes me think of standing on a high hill to look at the view. I prefer hills over mountains because mountains are often too cold and windy. Standing on top of a grassy hill and looking at the open, clear landscape makes me feel connected to the past, when the earth was untouched.

Ultimately, being myself is the most important thing I can do. Some people might disagree with Emerson, but to me, his words make perfect sense. The world is always trying to force us to conform, so resisting this pressure and staying true to who you are is indeed one of the greatest accomplishments. This is why I fully support Emerson's message.
