Students do not get the same benefits from studying at home as they do from attending school in person. Traditional schools offer many opportunities that online learning simply cannot match. While everyone has different learning styles, attending regular classes is generally a much better option. It allows students to choose the subjects they prefer and offers numerous advantages. By going to a physical school, students can meet new people, participate in extracurricular clubs, and get direct support from their teachers.

First of all, attending a traditional school gives students the chance to socialize. Most people do not want to be isolated or lonely; having friends to talk to and confide in is very important. School provides a social environment where you can interact with many peers and build lasting friendships. For instance, a student named Generic_Name once had to choose between online learning and regular school. She chose to study at home because she liked the idea of not waking up early. Although she enjoyed it for the first few weeks, she soon realized she felt completely isolated and had no friends. After discussing her loneliness with her mother, who pointed out that this was a result of distance learning, Generic_Name decided to return to a regular school. This shows that physical classes help students avoid loneliness by helping them make friends.

In addition, physical schools offer various clubs and extracurricular activities, which are usually unavailable in distance learning. Public schools provide a wide range of activities that students can enjoy and use to prepare for their future. For example, a student who loves sports can join the school football team. Being part of a team can even lead to athletic scholarships and opportunities in major leagues. Furthermore, participating in school clubs helps students discover new interests, gain valuable experience, and figure out what career path they want to pursue later in life.

Some people might argue that online learning is better because it allows students to work jobs, stay out of trouble, or look after younger siblings. However, attending physical classes means students can get direct help from their teachers. The truth is that not everyone can understand difficult subjects easily on their own; we often need guidance from someone with more knowledge. Fortunately, in traditional schools, teachers are often willing to stay after hours to help students with challenging assignments. Even if classrooms can sometimes be noisy or distracting, teachers are there to discuss grades, offer advice for improvement, and provide deep, face-to-face explanations that make learning much easier.

In conclusion, attending school in person allows students to make friends, try new activities, and improve their grades with the help of teachers. Although some people may dislike public schools, they are often the best option for a student's development. Going to school is a great way to get out of the house for a few hours, as staying home all day can become boring. School offers unique experiences, like sharing lunch with friends and having fun while learning. Ultimately, after-school activities keep students safe and help them choose a positive path in life, proving that traditional education offers a perfect balance of fun and learning.

This is not just my personal opinion as a student; this change would negatively affect everyone in the school community. Longer days would lead to behavioral issues because students get restless when stuck in one place for too long. Furthermore, academic performance would suffer, as exhausted students cannot focus properly. If the school day is extended, students will also lack the time needed to complete homework and prepare for exams.

This decision does not only impact students; it also creates difficulties for teachers. Teachers have their own lives and children, and longer hours would prevent them from spending quality time with their families. Additionally, many students have regular appointments. For example, I have monthly orthodontist visits that must be scheduled in the morning, causing me to miss several classes and fall behind on schoolwork. If school hours were not increased, I could easily schedule these appointments in the afternoon. When students are sick or miss school, a longer day means they have an even heavier workload to catch up on.

The school itself would face several negative consequences. Financially, the school would have to spend more money on extra food, paper, restroom supplies, and new student planners with additional hall passes. Moreover, staff would have to deal with more behavioral issues and arguments among tired students. Another major concern is safety on the roads. If the school day is extended by an hour and a half, our dismissal time would coincide with elementary schools. This would lead to congested roads, too many school buses at once, and a higher risk of traffic accidents.

Most students already wake up very early. Adding more hours to the day would cause extreme exhaustion, making it nearly impossible for students to absorb lessons. Teachers would also struggle to deliver quality lessons when they are tired. It is crucial for the school board to reconsider this proposal and listen to the viewpoints of the students. I am certainly not alone in thinking this is a bad idea that harms everyone involved.

In conclusion, extending the school day is a mistake because of the negative effects on students, teachers, and the school system. It would exhaust students and hinder their learning, while also making teachers more tired and easily frustrated. This would inevitably lead to more conflicts and administrative problems. I strongly urge the school board to rethink this plan and consider the perspectives of those who will be most affected.

Is it more beneficial to work in a group or by yourself? In my opinion, collaborating with a group is much more advantageous for several reasons. First, you can receive assistance from your peers when you are stuck. Second, you do not have to complete the entire project alone because you can divide the tasks among the members. Finally, you can gain a deeper understanding of the subject. Let me explain these points in more detail.

To begin with, working in a team is excellent because your partners can support you with difficult assignments. If you are having trouble, a group member can notice your struggle and offer assistance. They can explain the problem clearly so that you truly comprehend it, often sharing different methods and strategies to find the solution. For instance, in my math class, the teacher paired me with a friend for an assignment. I did not understand the topic at all, but my friend sat down with me and explained how to solve the problems. She showed me several different ways to do the work, and without her help, I would have remained completely confused.

Another major advantage of group work is that every person can be assigned a specific task. When everyone has a particular role, the project gets done much faster. You do not have to worry about doing all the work yourself, which reduces stress because your teammates are responsible for their own parts. For example, last week in history class, I worked in a group with three classmates. We divided the work: Chloe gathered the information, Marcus found relevant images, Sean searched for supporting videos, and I was responsible for the citations. Because of this teamwork, we completed the assignment before the end of class and received an A.

Finally, collaborating with others allows you to learn much more about the topic. Your group members might discover facts or ideas that you were not aware of before. This exchange of information gives everyone new perspectives, making the subject easier to understand. Furthermore, this shared knowledge is very helpful when preparing for upcoming quizzes and exams, as you have already discussed the material and answered questions together.

In conclusion, working in a group offers many more benefits than working alone. It allows you to get help when you are confused, share the workload so you are not overwhelmed, and learn new information from your peers. Trying to complete everything by yourself can be very difficult, whereas being part of a team provides clear advantages that lead to better results.

Should teenagers have a curfew? Keeping young people safe is incredibly important, especially at night when the world can be dangerous. Currently, a local city council is discussing whether to introduce a teen curfew. This debate raises several questions. If this law is passed, does it mean any teenager outside after hours is committing a crime? Will curfews actually protect teenagers, or will they just limit their freedom?

The city council is considering this curfew for a few key reasons. First, they want to prevent teenagers from getting hurt or putting themselves in dangerous situations. Second, they want to shield young people from the negative influences in society. Finally, they want to reduce trouble, as some teenagers make poor decisions, such as drinking alcohol, when they are unsupervised. These concerns are driving the council's discussion.

If the curfew is approved, would being outside late mean a teenager is breaking the law? People have different views on this, and the answer largely depends on the situation. For instance, if a teenager is out because of work or an emergency, they should not be considered lawbreakers. The same applies if they are accompanied by an adult. On the other hand, if they are just hanging out with friends or going to parties, then they would indeed be violating the curfew. Therefore, whether it is illegal depends on their reason for being out.

Does a curfew keep teenagers safe, or does it unfairly disrupt their lives? Naturally, most teenagers feel that a curfew interferes with their social lives and stops them from having fun. However, a curfew is necessary to keep them safe from unexpected dangers. Additionally, it discourages teenagers from sneaking out of their homes at night without their parents' knowledge, which is highly risky. Young people need to ask themselves if taking such risks is truly worth it, as dangerous situations can happen when least expected.

In conclusion, the debate over a teenage curfew involves strong arguments on both sides. The main goal of the proposed law is to protect young people from harm and trouble. While teenagers might view the curfew as an annoying restriction on their freedom, parents and officials see it as a vital safety measure. Ultimately, the law should be flexible, distinguishing between acceptable reasons for being out, like work, and unacceptable ones, like partying.

The AVID program is an incredibly enjoyable educational activity for anyone who has a dream they want to achieve. First of all, this program does not just help you grow as an individual, but it also motivates you to pursue a college education. Furthermore, it offers helpful tutorials that assess your current academic level and guide you to improve in all your subjects. On top of that, students get the chance to go on exciting and educational field trips. Finally, being in AVID feels like having a second family that supports you wherever you go.

In AVID, you learn how to be a responsible and diligent student. For instance, weekly binder checks teach you how to stay organized. Although it is structured like a regular class, everyone in AVID shares a common ambition to succeed, and we encourage each other never to give up until we reach our goals. While not every teenager thinks about college, many of us do. However, hanging out with the wrong crowd can easily pull you down and ruin your future. It is fine to be friendly with different people, but it is important not to get dragged into bad habits that could distract you from your dreams.

Additionally, tutorials are a fundamental part of the AVID experience. They allow you to show your teachers and classmates how much effort you are putting into your studies. During these sessions, you stand in front of a small group to explain an academic problem you are struggling with, which helps you learn from your classmates' feedback. It is a great way to share knowledge and collaborate. These tutorials also help build your confidence. Even if some students are naturally quiet and prefer to listen rather than speak, participating in these groups helps everyone step out of their comfort zone.

Another wonderful benefit of AVID is the opportunity to go on field trips, which many other students do not get to experience. We visit different college campuses to learn about higher education, explore the grounds with guides, and meet new people. These trips are both educational and highly entertaining. To make things even better, we organize fundraisers to pay for fun trips to places like King's Dominion. Working hard without any rewards can make you lose motivation, so having these fun trips keeps us driven. Just as my niece inspires me to do my best, the reward of riding roller coasters with friends at the end of the year motivates AVID students to keep taking Cornell notes and studying hard.

Most importantly, AVID functions as a close-knit family. We all support each other, and there is no room for negativity or judgment. Even though we come from diverse backgrounds, we treat each other with kindness and stay united. If any student feels like quitting, the rest of the group is there to lift them up and keep them going. Our shared motto is "dream, believe, achieve." This supportive environment helps you succeed in school while making both yourself and your parents proud.

In conclusion, AVID is a highly rewarding program because it allows you to make new friends, participate in unique activities, and join a community that feels like family. For students who might not have a strong support system at home, AVID provides a safe space where you can truly be yourself. Joining this program is a risk worth taking because it can guide you toward a bright, positive future and help you become the successful person you want to be.

After graduating, they must face intense job interviews to stand out from other candidates and start paying off their student debts. This difficult reality is overcome by hard work and determination, not by simply staying positive.

In conclusion, a successful life is built on reaching your goals, finishing your education, and finding a suitable career through effort. In the end, a positive attitude will not take you anywhere without the hard work to back it up.

Online Learning

Who doesn't want to be left in the house all day using an electronic device with online access? Although students save money and time by taking classes from home. It is not beneficial to learn online because students lose focus of what they are learning and tend to easily get distracted when they're in their house, students can't have a one on one conversation with a teacher nor discuss with classmates, and students could also face technical difficulties when attending online classes from home.

Losing focus has a big impact in learning. For example, my friend Generic_Name sent me a text message last month, right when I started studying for my history mid-term exam. I responded back to Generic_Name's text, and without realizing we kept on messaging past midnight. This shows how easily students get distracted at home with a cellular device and how easy it is to lose focus. The next morning I decided to get to school an hour early and review one on one with my teacher.

Secondly, taking classes online doesn't just mean you don't have a physical teacher or instructor that you can question lively, but also means that it will be challenging to find answers to your questions. I remember in my sophomore year a kid in our econ class named Generic_Name was really sick for a while so he had ended up taking classes online. Generic_Name was a straight A student, always was first to answer the teachers questions and he also used to ask questions. Thankfully Generic_Name healed towards the end of the year and I asked him if he benefited and if he recommends attending classes from home. The straight A student Generic_Name said it was a real challenge to take the class online and he finished the class a month after he should have with a B- average. Generic_Name had also said that one of the most difficult parts about attending a class online was his laptop not functioning at all times, and not having a teacher you can talk and converse with one on one.

Finally, using your personal computer and internet connection can always be an issue. You can't always depend on your computer, not just the computers but even people aren't perfect. Another main problem Generic_Name had when attending classes online was his laptop and network connection. Generic_Name explained that he always faced technical difficulties. When his laptop wasn't functioning right, the only thing he could do was to stop the lesson and wait for his dad to get the laptop repaired, which took time. Each month, either his laptop or internet connection would not cooperate, so he finished the class a month later than everyone.

In conclusion, Everyone would like to save money and time by taking classes from home. But getting distracted, not asking your teacher questions when you need to, and wasting money on laptop repair is not worth it at all. Learning from a far distance could also be an option but when asking if it is beneficial, we can say that it is not by looking at the listed reasoning.

Asking for advice from several people can help us make much better decisions. By doing this, we can see things from different perspectives, find more choices, and discover better ways to solve our problems. In fact, if we only rely on one person's opinion, things can easily go wrong.

To begin with, gathering various viewpoints is a great reason to seek multiple opinions. For instance, imagine a girl named Jane who went to a large shopping mall to find a specific store she really wanted to visit. When she arrived, she got lost and asked a stranger for directions. The man told her the store was on the second floor. However, after going upstairs and searching in vain, she decided to ask someone else. This second person told her the store was actually on the first floor, right next to the ice cream parlor. Jane followed this advice, bought an ice cream, and easily found the shop. If she had not asked for a second opinion, she would have given up and never found it.

Furthermore, having more than one source of information is always safer. Consider another scenario where Jane was starting her first day at a new high school, and neither she nor her parents knew where her classroom was. Her parents suggested she just follow the other students. She spotted a girl who looked like a student and followed her, but they ended up going in completely different directions, leaving Jane lost in the hallways. Instead of panicking, Jane began asking several different students for directions. By getting multiple answers that pointed to the same location, she finally figured out where to go. If she had only trusted her first choice, she would have ended up in the wrong classroom.

Finally, seeking multiple opinions is crucial for solving dangerous problems. For example, Jane was hosting a sleepover with two friends, and they decided to cook in the kitchen even though her mother had told them not to. Suddenly, the oven caught fire, and Jane started to panic. One of her friends suggested throwing water on the flames, while the other friend insisted they call emergency services immediately. Jane realized that calling 911 was the much safer option. The firefighters arrived quickly and put out the fire. If she had listened to the bad advice of throwing water on an oven fire, the situation could have been a disaster.

People often say that you should not judge a book by its cover, and this is especially true when it comes to human relationships. In this context, the "cover" represents the first impression we make on others. Just like a book cover, a first impression does not always reflect what is truly inside. It is only after we start "reading" the person—or getting to know them—that we realize appearances can be deceptive. Many factors influence the initial image we project to others. Differences in personality, temporary situations, and how we present ourselves mean that first impressions are often the worst way to judge someone.

An individual's personality plays a major role in the first impression they create. Although everyone is unique, initial judgments often depend on whether a person is shy or outgoing. For instance, I met my best friend after moving to a new high school during my junior year. Before we actually spoke, she never said a word to anyone in class, which made me think she was a bit strange. However, I soon realized that I behaved the exact same way because of my own quiet nature. I knew that I was a shy person who only showed my true colors after getting comfortable with someone, so I thought she might be the same. As we began talking a little more each day, our friendship grew, and I discovered she was not strange at all. Like me, she was actually an outgoing person hidden behind a wall of shyness. Many people put up a quiet, reserved barrier when meeting strangers. Consequently, judging someone based on a first impression can lead to completely wrong conclusions, as a shy person might actually be very social once they feel comfortable.

Furthermore, first impressions are unreliable because we rarely know what kind of situation another person is going through. When we meet someone for the first time, we have no idea if they are having a terrible day, dealing with personal difficulties, or coping with a major disappointment. They might be grieving a loss or simply trying to manage the stressful routines of daily life. Under these circumstances, people often build a protective wall around themselves, and making a good impression on a stranger is usually the last thing on their mind.

I experienced this myself on my first day of senior year. I hurried to my first classroom, even though I had plenty of time. When I entered, my only focus was finding a seat immediately, regardless of who was sitting nearby. At lunchtime, I sat alone and ate quickly so I could get to my next class on time. I was so anxious about being late, finding my way around, and doing everything correctly that I did not even think about making a good impression on my classmates. As a result, my peers got the impression that I was nervous and unsociable. In reality, my behavior was entirely caused by the stressful situation I was facing at that moment.

In conclusion, numerous factors shape the first impression we have of someone. A person's personality, their current circumstances, and how they happen to behave in a specific moment all affect how we perceive them initially. Because our quick judgments are based on these temporary factors, first impressions are frequently incorrect. If we based all of our relationships on these initial moments, we would have far fewer friends in the world. Ultimately, first impressions are a poor way to judge others. It is only when we take the time to truly know someone that we can understand their real character and appreciate them for who they are, rather than judging them by their "cover."

However, if they decide to withdraw their child from an activity, they just need to inform the school guidance counselor and the activity leader.

On the other hand, if a student begins to fail classes or their grades start dropping, the school counselor should intervene. They should meet with the student to find out what is wrong. If the student is overwhelmed by too many activities, they should discuss which ones to drop temporarily until their grades improve. This approach motivates students to keep their grades up if they want to continue participating in their favorite clubs.

Finally, if a student's attendance at meetings is poor and inconsistent, they should face consequences. For example, students should not miss more than five meetings a month without a valid reason. If they exceed this limit, they could be suspended from the club for a period of time or even removed completely, with their parents being notified of the decision.

In conclusion, schools should have minimal control over a student's extracurricular activities. Families should have the primary authority in these decisions. The school should only intervene under specific circumstances, such as when a student's grades begin to slip or when their attendance at club meetings becomes unacceptable.

Although year-round schools offer more frequent breaks throughout the year, they significantly reduce summer vacation time. This calendar system ultimately leads to increased stress, shorter holidays, and fewer opportunities to earn money during the summer months.

The first major problem with year-round schooling is the high level of stress it causes. For students, daily pressure often comes from deciding what to wear, leading them to buy unnecessary clothes just to avoid repeating outfits and to look good in front of their peers. However, students are not the only ones suffering. Teachers also face immense pressure because they must constantly plan lessons and grade assignments without a proper rest period.

Another disadvantage is the reduction of summer vacation. With only a three-to-four-week summer break, students do not get the long holiday they desire. This short period is not enough time to travel abroad for an extended family vacation. Consequently, parents are also affected because responsible parents cannot easily travel overseas while leaving their children behind.

Furthermore, year-round schedules limit the ability to earn money. Students cannot work effectively over the summer because one month is simply not enough time to earn a significant income compared to a traditional three-month break. Additionally, it is not just students who lose money; the government and school districts also face higher expenses because they must pay for electricity, water, and other utility bills throughout the entire year.

While some people argue that having multiple short breaks during the year is beneficial, this does not make up for the loss of a long summer vacation. Others believe that shorter breaks prevent students from forgetting what they have learned. However, studying continuously without a substantial summer rest ultimately results in extreme stress for everyone involved.

The writer Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated that staying true to yourself in a world that constantly tries to change you is a major achievement. I completely agree with this idea because resisting social pressure is incredibly difficult. For instance, back in the eighth grade, a person I considered a close friend wanted me to change my personality because they felt I was not cool enough to associate with. Although I initially blamed myself, I eventually realized that real friends will always accept you for who you are. Indeed, embracing your true identity is one of the hardest challenges, often because we are too shy, insecure, or terrified of other people's opinions.

For a long time, I struggled with low self-esteem and felt I was never good enough. I kept my painful emotions hidden inside, even experiencing dark thoughts of ending my life because I felt so hopeless. To cope, I pretended to be fine until I almost convinced myself I was happy, but this false front did not last. Fortunately, now that I am in the eleventh grade, I have met someone special—my current girlfriend—who brings genuine joy into my life and allows me to be my true self. This experience made me realize how lucky I am. Ultimately, Emerson was right; staying authentic is a massive triumph because the world is full of obstacles and people who do not want to see you succeed.

I am very capable of doing a school project by myself.

However, even I could use some one else's input in the matter.

I believe working together as a group is beneficial .

For example, my friend Generic_Name he is a very smart person.

He was on the top of the class with grades but, even he could not do it by himself.

One day the teacher assigned us projects.

Generic_Name decided to do it alone.

On the due date, which was later that week Generic_Name turned in the project.

The teacher told him he failed he did not understand why.

The teacher later on the day took him aside and explained that he was not understanding the question.

He asked her how he could make up the points for the failed project.

Two weeks after that she assigned another project.

She took Generic_Name aside and said ' this time work with somebody".

Generic_Name listed so he asked somebody to work with him.

The day the project was due, he was nervous because he does not work with people often.

The teacher told him they got a perfect score.

She told him he passed because when you have more than just one persons input.

I picked a friend of mine, Generic_Name.

I strongly believe that working in a group is much more beneficial for students than working alone. Even though my friend Generic_Name and I are both very capable of completing school assignments on our own, we have both realized that everyone needs help and feedback from others at some point. Collaborative work offers valuable support and different perspectives that individual work simply cannot match.

I highly recommend asking your teachers for more group projects and discussing with your parents how these collaboration skills are useful in the real world. You will be surprised by how much easier your life becomes when you share the decision-making process with others.

Technology has both positive and negative sides, with some aspects being highly beneficial to humans and others quite destructive. In my opinion, reducing human contact because of technology has a very negative impact on our lives. It can lead to depression and isolation, make people lose touch with reality, and seriously damage both physical and mental health.

To begin with, technology can easily trigger depression and isolation, which is a dangerous combination. For instance, many young people experience cyberbullying on social media, which leads to severe emotional distress. Consequently, these teenagers often isolate themselves and refuse to go to school. In conclusion, technology is causing many terrible problems in our lives, often without us even realizing it. To begin with, science is an incredibly fun subject for both children and adults. The main reason for this excitement is the opportunity to conduct various experiments. For instance, if you want to teach students about kinetic and potential energy, you can design an experiment where they actually throw a ball to visualize these concepts in action. Additionally, science is enjoyable because it is a shared experience. When one student performs an experiment, the entire class gets to observe and enjoy the results together. Finally, creating a science lesson is exciting because it encourages students to talk to one another and share their observations. For example, during an egg drop experiment, students can compare their designs with their peers, learning from both their successes and their mistakes. Therefore, the hands-on nature of science makes it a highly entertaining subject.

Secondly, science is one of the easiest subjects to teach to young learners. Unlike other subjects, it does not require students to constantly memorize complex information. For example, in English, students must memorize root words, and in math, they have to remember various formulas. In science, however, they only need to understand basic terminology to get started. Another reason science is simple to grasp is that it relies on experiments, which are easy to follow as long as students pay attention. While math requires endless practice to master a concept, science allows students to understand a process just by watching it happen. Furthermore, science is highly visual and often involves drawing pictures, which is one of the easiest ways for children to learn. The impact of technology on our daily lives is a widely debated topic, with many people questioning whether its influence is positive or negative. In my opinion, technology is highly beneficial because almost everything we need is now available online. It allows us to read digital books, connect with others instantly using laptops or smartphones, and write documents easily. Although the news often highlights the negative aspects of technology, it actually brings many advantages to our lives.

For instance, many people do not have the time to visit a physical bookstore to search for a specific book. Today, almost all books are available online, making reading much faster and more convenient. During long road trips, you can easily read on your smartphone or tablet to pass the time. Busy parents who rarely get a moment to relax can enjoy a book while their children are sleeping in the car. Since digital books are stored on our devices, they are easy to carry and impossible to lose. Furthermore, e-readers automatically save your page, allow you to bookmark important sections, and even provide instant definitions or translations for unfamiliar words.

Technology also makes it much easier to stay in touch with friends and family who live in other states or countries. Instead of writing a letter and waiting a week or more for a reply, we can use video chat on our tablets or laptops. Email is another great tool that allows us to send drafts of our work to others for quick feedback and editing. Additionally, video calls allow multiple people to connect at the same time from anywhere in the world, making it easy to catch up even when everyone has a busy schedule.

As technology continues to advance, it will become even more integrated into our lives. Currently, devices like tablets, laptops, and smartphones are very popular and fun to use. Although these gadgets are expensive and require careful handling, they are worth the investment. In the near future, we will likely see even more advanced technology, and digital devices might completely replace traditional paper and pencils.

Many people support this technological growth because it improves our daily activities, especially education. Even young children now use tablets to learn basic skills like the alphabet and numbers. Many schools provide laptops or tablets to students to ensure they have the necessary tools to complete their schoolwork. Students enjoy using technology because it allows them to research information for projects and watch educational videos that explain difficult topics clearly.

In conclusion, technology is an excellent tool for communication and daily tasks. It offers simple solutions to many of our problems and will undoubtedly play an even larger role in our future. While some people might miss using traditional paper and pencils, digital tools provide a faster, safer, and more efficient way to connect with the world. We should embrace these changes as technology continues to improve our lives.

Because of this, I strongly disagree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s ideas about extreme individuality. In my own life, I have essential people like my parents, my sister, and close friends who are just like family. Having these connections is crucial because they make life's journey much easier and help us grow as we get older. If we cut ourselves off from everyone else, we would end up living a very lonely and isolated life. We need to trust and rely on one another to get through difficult times.

I experienced this myself when I was between twelve and fourteen years old. Back then, I struggled with my school grades and felt very anxious every day. I was worried that I could not motivate myself to do better or make friends. During that time, I only focused on myself, which made me feel depressed and unhappy. Everything changed when I realized that I could not do it all alone and needed to accept help from others. By surrounding myself with supportive people, I slowly managed to improve. We change ourselves simply by living alongside others, and even if we do not notice the transformation happening, it is a wonderful thing.

Another disadvantage of complete isolation is that life becomes very boring. Without anyone around, you have no one to talk to or share moments with. On the other hand, having friends and meeting new people makes life exciting and fun. Together, you can play games, travel, and share experiences that teach you valuable life lessons. Some people believe that society is cold and that nobody cares about them, but this is often because they have had bad experiences. Negative influences can make people fearful or bitter, leading them to isolate themselves. However, the solution is simply to open up, ask for help, and allow others into your life.

In conclusion, extreme individuality can be harmful and lead to a lonely path. We need other people in our lives to support us and lift us up, because everyone has value. While we must never let others dictate who we are, we should also avoid isolating ourselves. You are the main character of your own story, but your life is much richer when you share it with others.

Human survival and progress have always depended on our ability to cooperate and share responsibilities. Throughout history, we have achieved incredible things, like building complex structures and traveling across oceans, which would be impossible for a single person to do alone. This proves that collaboration is essential, as two heads are indeed better than one.

When you join a team, it is because you have specific skills that contribute to a shared goal. For instance, if you work for a company that designs websites, you might use your skills in coding or graphic design to create content. In this scenario, you act like a carefully chosen cog in a larger machine. When everyone fits together perfectly, the entire system runs smoothly and efficiently without putting too much pressure on any single part.

Furthermore, working in a group ensures that the workload is distributed fairly. Just as construction workers carefully measure and divide materials like cement to avoid waste, a team divides tasks so that no single member becomes overwhelmed. We can see this clearly in a professional kitchen: one person peels the vegetables, another prepares the cake batter, and a third adds the decorations. Everyone has a specific job that matches their capacity.

In conclusion, teamwork offers countless benefits and relies heavily on clear communication. When a team functions like a well-oiled machine, the members work together as a single unit. Because everyone focuses on their specific task—just like the kitchen staff peeling, mixing, and decorating—errors are minimized. Ultimately, cooperation is one of our most valuable lessons, because there will always be challenges we cannot face alone.

The statement is "the first impression is almost impossible to change" which is a different feeling for everybody, but for me, I disagree. In fact, the first impression is really important and sometimes true, but I think the first impression does not define a person, an object or a situation. Having a first impression is a human reflex, like having an opinion or a judgment. We are doing it unconsciously.

The first impression is most of the time not real, you need to search deeper to make an opinion and when you really have an opinion, then, the first impression is not important anymore. For example, when you meet someone, your first impression might be that you think she is supercilious and even a little bit mean. Therefore when you really get to know her deeper then you will find that she just had a bad day and that she is nice and sociable. Sometimes it's the contrary, a person seems really nice but in reality she is not, so your first impression was wrong. It is not good to stay on a first impression because most of the time it's wrong.

Moreover, the physic, behaviors or attitude can change an impression. If the person do not smile and seems to be rude but in reality is the nicest person, then it will be awkward for you because you thought she was bad. Sometimes a person can have a bad reputation because of the first impression he shows and it is not his fault, some persons just don't smile every time. Sometimes you can be disappointed because you didn't get to know the person because of your first impression.

The first impressions is not only for people but also for a situation or an object. For example if you are in a library and you want to buy a book, the first thing you are going to do is looking at the cover of the book. If it's pretty you will more easily choose this one instead of a book with a black cover and only the title, because it is your first impression. But your first impression is wrong because you didn't take time to read the resume and you will find soon that the pretty book is actually boring instead of the black book which is really interesting. An object can look nice but have a bad quality. The first impression is the color and the shape of the object, like the physic and the attitude of a person.

In conclusion I would say that the first impression is sometimes right but most of the time it's not. In my opinion, you must not keep in mind your first impression of a person, it's most of the time wrong. You have to get to know the person to build your own opinion. It is normal to have a first impression, like judging, but you must not take the habit to stick with your first impression.

People have different views on the idea that first impressions are nearly impossible to alter, but I personally disagree with this statement. Although initial reactions are significant and can occasionally be accurate, they do not truly define a person, an object, or a situation. Forming a first impression is simply a natural human reflex, much like making an automatic judgment, and we usually do it without even realizing it.

Most of the time, our initial thoughts about someone are not accurate, and we need to look deeper to form a genuine opinion. Once we truly understand someone, that initial reaction loses its importance. For instance, when meeting someone new, you might initially think they are arrogant or unfriendly. However, once you get to know them better, you might realize they were simply having a difficult day, and they are actually very kind and outgoing. The opposite can also happen: someone who seems extremely pleasant at first might turn out to be quite different. Relying solely on our first thoughts is a mistake because they are frequently incorrect.

Furthermore, a person's physical appearance, behavior, or attitude can easily mislead us. If someone does not smile, they might seem impolite, but they could actually be a wonderful person. Realizing this later can make you feel embarrassed for judging them too quickly. Some people get a bad reputation simply because they do not smile constantly, which is unfair to them. Ultimately, if we let our initial judgments guide us, we might miss the chance to make a great friend and end up feeling disappointed.

This concept does not only apply to people, but also to objects and situations. For example, if you are looking for a book in a library, you will probably notice the cover first. You might easily choose a book with an attractive cover over a plain black one that only displays the title. However, this choice based on appearance can be wrong if you do not read the summary. You might soon discover that the beautiful book is actually quite dull, while the plain one is highly engaging. Just like a person's looks and attitude, an object's shape and color can create a positive first impression, even if the actual quality is poor.

In conclusion, while first impressions can occasionally be correct, they are usually misleading. In my view, we should not hold onto our initial thoughts about others because they are often mistaken. Instead, we must take the time to get to know people before forming a final opinion. While it is natural to make quick judgments, we should avoid the habit of letting these initial reactions dictate how we treat others.

Additionally, a student using a phone can easily distract the person sitting next to them, interrupting their classmates' concentration.

When students constantly play on their phones, they ignore their lessons and fail to learn. Instead of thinking critically and absorbing information, they simply search for quick answers online. Can curfews really stop teenagers from getting into trouble? Currently, the city council is debating whether to introduce a curfew for minors, set at 10:00 p.m. on weekdays and midnight on weekends. Under this proposal, being out past these hours would be against the law. Although we might not always agree with every law, we still have a responsibility to follow them. Personally, I believe the city council should approve this curfew for minors. When it comes to young people, their safety must be our main priority, and having a curfew is the best way to protect them. We must take into account the many dangers that exist in our world today.

Have you ever stopped to think about what could happen when your teenager is out late? There are many hazards in today's society, and while we hope nothing bad happens, the reality is that anything is possible. Without adult supervision, young people are much more vulnerable. Unfortunately, many minors are injured or even killed for reasons we cannot understand. Implementing a curfew is a practical way to protect your children from these dangers. Even though a midnight curfew on weekends still carries some risks, it is our duty to teach teenagers how to make safe choices. If we explain the importance of these rules, they will be more cautious. Of course, many teenagers will resist these limits; I know this from my own experience. When I was younger, I wanted to hang out with my friends and sometimes ignored my mother's rules. However, I eventually realized how much my safety mattered to her and how anxious she became whenever I stayed out late.

To illustrate this danger, consider the tragic story of Generic_Name in New York. He was an excellent teenager who loved spending time with his family and nephews. His mother explained that he rarely went out with friends and preferred to stay at home, where he was very close to his sister. He got excellent grades in school and never got into any trouble. However, he was tragically killed just a few blocks from his home, outside a small grocery store. It happened after dark, when a group of men spotted him, dragged him out of the store, and stabbed him. Although he cried out for help, nobody came to his aid. He tried to walk to the hospital but unfortunately collapsed and died on the sidewalk. The attackers were caught months later and admitted they had mistaken him for someone else. Generic_Name did absolutely nothing wrong, yet he lost his life. If he had waited until the next morning to go out, or if his mother had accompanied him, the outcome might have been completely different. This shows that walking alone at night is simply not safe, whereas being with a parent changes the situation entirely.

Some parents might argue that they want to give their children the freedom they never had when they were young. They may believe there is no harm in letting teenagers go out whenever they want, making a curfew unnecessary. While everyone wants to enjoy life to the fullest, doing so does not require being out past curfew. In fact, there is much more to see and do during the day. Furthermore, even if you trust your own child completely, you cannot trust the strangers they might encounter in public at night. The daytime is significantly safer than the dark night hours, largely because of the number of people around. If you are in danger during the day, you can scream for help, run away, or signal to bystanders. At night, however, most people are asleep, and the streets are practically empty, leaving no one to help you.

In conclusion, the city council needs to consider the real dangers of our world and make the right decision for our youth by establishing a curfew. Teenagers can still enjoy their freedom and live happy lives even with these boundaries in place. This policy would be a positive step forward, ensuring that young people remain safe. Ultimately, almost everyone agrees that protecting minors is a top priority, and a curfew is an effective tool to keep teenagers safe and out of trouble.

Some people may look friendly and polite, but they might eventually treat you poorly, leaving you disappointed because you trusted them based only on their pleasant demeanor. A lot of people believe that online learning is an excellent choice for students. This method of education offers several advantages, including improved attendance, fewer behavioral issues, and better accessibility for students with disabilities or medical conditions. Although some critics argue that staying home makes students lazy and irresponsible, distance learning actually brings great benefits to both students and schools.

To begin with, studying from home can significantly improve attendance rates. When students can join classes from their own houses, they are much less likely to skip school. One of the biggest challenges for teenagers is waking up very early to prepare for a long eight-hour school day, which often leaves them feeling exhausted and unmotivated. Online learning solves this problem.

Additionally, some children are born with or develop health conditions and disabilities that prevent them from going to a physical school building. Every child has a right to an education, and virtual learning makes this possible by bringing the classroom to their homes. While there are numerous advantages to online education, supporting these students is perhaps the most meaningful benefit of all.

Another major advantage is the reduction of social problems. In traditional schools, many students suffer from bullying and unnecessary social drama, which distracts them from their studies. By learning at home, students can avoid these negative interactions, allowing them to focus entirely on their education in a safe environment. Consequently, schools will also face fewer bullying issues.

Of course, some people worry that studying from home makes students undisciplined and lazy. However, students should have the freedom to choose how they learn. If a student becomes lazy, it is a personal issue rather than a fault of the system. In fact, many believe that managing their own schedule online actually teaches students to be more independent and responsible.

While we might never get a clear answer to this, the academic expectations remain the same.

While not all classmates are difficult to get along with, the social pressure can be overwhelming. Online learning is a very practical alternative, and if I had the opportunity, I would definitely choose to study from home.

Some research suggests that deciding on a dream career before high school can lead to greater professional success. However, forcing young people to make this choice creates an overwhelming amount of pressure. Committing to a specific career path at a very young age is a mistake. It causes unnecessary stress, prevents students from focusing on their personal growth, and ignores the fact that high school is a time when people naturally change their minds.

First of all, choosing a career early leads to high levels of stress throughout high school. While sticking to a single path might seem simple, it is actually very difficult. When you commit early, you constantly worry about whether you are making progress fast enough. This puts you in a difficult position that is hard to escape. You become so focused on one specific goal that it becomes hard to study or pay attention in your other classes. High school is a place where education is supposed to shape you, and you will likely want to change your direction. Therefore, students should not put themselves under this kind of pressure.

In addition, the pressure to succeed can be incredibly damaging. Many students feel they must stick to their chosen path just to make their parents, teachers, and school administrators proud. They want to prove that they are responsible and committed. However, as the weeks and months pass, this pressure only increases. Eventually, students can become sad or depressed because they realize they are pursuing a career to please others rather than to satisfy their own desires.

Furthermore, high school is a time of major transition, and it changes how everyone thinks. It is very different from middle school, and it is certainly not like the movies. The academic workload is more challenging, and there are many different elective courses to choose from. It is highly likely that your interests will change once you are exposed to these new subjects. It makes no sense to lock yourself into a career before you have even had the chance to discover what you truly enjoy.

In my opinion, committing to a career at a young age is not a good idea. Based on my own experiences and what I have seen in others, it is much better to explore. You should take various classes in high school to see what you enjoy, and if a subject does not interest you, simply try something else. Real life is not like television. Everyone develops at their own pace, and a career is just one part of life. Young people should not push themselves too hard, too soon.

Deciding on a career path during high school is a great way for students to prepare for their future. In some cultures, young people are expected to choose their profession before starting high school. Making this commitment at an early age is highly beneficial.

First of all, choosing a career in high school allows students to reach their goals much faster. For instance, if they begin studying and learning about a specific field early on, they can graduate from college sooner. Instead of spending the traditional four years in university, they might finish in just one or two years. This is because they will already have acquired foundational knowledge from their high school classes.

In addition, this early focus helps students develop a more mature and serious attitude toward their future. Taking specialized courses can motivate them to strive for a better life. It can change their perspective, helping them realize that they are responsible for their own success. Ultimately, it teaches them that building a career is essential for moving forward in life.

On the other hand, some people believe that choosing a career so early is not a good idea. They argue that it is a waste of time and puts too much pressure on teenagers. Students might have to worry about extra classes and heavier workloads, which can lead to physical and mental exhaustion. Consequently, these critics believe it is better to wait until college.

However, waiting until college can be a mistake because students will not have enough time to carefully consider their options. When they enter university, they need to select a major immediately. Without prior preparation, they might choose a path they do not actually enjoy. This often results in spending extra years in college or dropping out entirely, which can negatively impact their future job prospects.

In conclusion, committing to a career at a young age is a very positive step. It prepares students for what lies ahead and helps them achieve their dreams much sooner. Furthermore, it gives them a clear idea of what to expect in higher education. Deciding on a career early supports students in many different ways, ensuring a brighter future.

Education plays a crucial role in preparing young people for our rapidly changing world. It shapes how future generations solve problems and make decisions, leading to historic achievements from space exploration to solving global crises. However, when it comes to the daily school schedule, I believe that school boards should not extend the school day. The current seven-hour schedule is already sufficient for academic and personal growth. Extending this time would only lead to more stress and unproductive behavior, while also creating major scheduling conflicts for students, parents, and school staff.

To begin with, the existing seven-hour school day is already packed with academic and emotional challenges. From the moment students arrive—sometimes dealing with late buses or waiting outside—their day is intense. They must focus on complex concepts in class, complete assignments, and manage daily school life, such as dealing with messy lockers or rushing between periods. By the end of the day, students are often exhausted and stressed about upcoming projects and social dynamics. Adding more time to this already demanding routine would only increase their mental fatigue.

Furthermore, lengthening the school day would likely worsen these daily struggles and introduce new problems. Students would probably face a heavier workload, including more classwork and homework. Sitting in classrooms for longer periods can also lead to boredom and a loss of focus, making the extra time unproductive. Additionally, adjusting the daily schedule to fit this extension might shorten certain periods or make the day feel incredibly tedious, leaving students feeling overwhelmed by tasks that seem impossible to finish.

Another major concern is how a longer school day would disrupt the schedules of everyone involved. Many students participate in extracurricular activities, such as baseball or swim team, which require significant time after school. If the school day is extended, these activities will be pushed later, leaving less time for family and rest. For parents, a shift in the school schedule could conflict with their work hours, making it difficult to pick up their children or manage family routines. Finally, school faculty and staff would also suffer. Teachers and custodians would have to stay even later to grade papers, prepare lessons, or clean the building, leading to a severe imbalance in their work-life schedules.

Of course, there are some potential benefits to a longer school day. Proponents argue that it allows for deeper study of subjects, gives students more time to finish homework before going home, and offers longer lunch or gym periods for socializing. However, these advantages do not outweigh the drawbacks. Even with more time, the risk of burnout and unproductive behavior remains high, meaning that a longer day does not guarantee better results.

In conclusion, I strongly oppose extending the academic schedule. The current seven-hour day is already full of activities and learning opportunities that demand a lot of energy from students. Changing this system would disrupt parents' work schedules, increase student stress through extra homework, and exhaust the teaching staff. While a longer day might seem beneficial on paper, the negative consequences on the well-being of students and families would be significant and difficult to reverse. Therefore, the school schedule should remain as it is.

Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators think that summer break is too long and students do not retain information as easily as they would in the fall. Because of this a lot of educators think we should have year- round school years. This would be shorter breaks in the summer (3-4 weeks) and longer more spread-out breaks throughout the year. I disagree with this statement and believe that summer break should stay the way it is.

The first reason I disagree with this statement is that it would ruin certain summer activities or even business plans. Think about all the activities in the summer that kids usually take part in, this could be sports, some sort of trip, etc. All of these activities students would preferably do during summer break. They have this preference because they see the summer as a perfect time to do all these activities without having to balance their education as well. They can put most of their time on this activity. The same preference applies to things like summer jobs or internships. During the summer they can learn important values like how to save and earn money. Or if a certain student has a chosen career path they can explore this career path by going in a internship for that spesicifc job. For all of these activities students at the very least would be discouraged to participate in if there was a year-round school year.

The second and probably most important reason is pertaining to the students mental health. An article, by Complex News writing about kids mental health stated, that over 40% of kids by the end of their freshmen year in high school are depressed or overall feel exhausted and depleted mentally. The article continues to say that this number from the time of their freshmen year only increases after each school year. Students use the summer break as a way for their brain to refresh from the long almost ten month school year. Students need this time to relax their brain and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain goes into this state where I am mostly just focused on school work. And I can admit that my brain at multiple points during the year is worn down and damaged by always be in this state. My brain does not get a chance to heal from this until the summer, when school is over. So if we were to hypothetically have a year-round school year, this would mean that the brain would also be in this damaged state year round. If this were the case than the brain of the student would eventually just break and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year- round school year.

Although the strongest reason for this year-round school year is that students cannot properly retain enough information for the next school year, I think I have a much stronger counter claim and solution to this problem. A very simple way to take care of the problem of retaining information, is to make mandatory (but simple) assignments from the previous year for the student to complete so that they don't forget this information. This way students can have their long summer break to refresh their brain and do their activities, without them having to forget any information. You get the best of both worlds with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion I think my assertions for the summer break to stay the way it is is much stronger than year-round school year argument. Having a year-round school year would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone said once upon a time "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."

While many students look forward to summer vacation, some teachers argue that this break is too long, causing students to forget what they learned by the time autumn arrives. Consequently, these educators suggest transitioning to a year-round school calendar, which features shorter summer breaks of three to four weeks and longer, more frequent holidays throughout the year. However, I disagree with this proposal and believe that the traditional summer break should be preserved.

First of all, changing the school calendar would disrupt valuable summer activities and employment opportunities. During the traditional summer break, young people participate in sports, family trips, and other recreational activities. They prefer doing these during a long break because they can focus entirely on them without the stress of schoolwork. Furthermore, summer is an ideal time for teenagers to get seasonal jobs or internships. Working teaches them financial responsibility, such as how to earn and save money, while internships allow them to explore potential career paths. If schools operated year-round, students would be much less likely to participate in these beneficial experiences.

Secondly, and most importantly, a long summer break is crucial for students' mental health. According to an article by Complex News, over 40% of high school freshmen experience depression or mental exhaustion, and this percentage continues to rise in later grades. Students need the summer months to recover from the intense pressure of a ten-month academic year. From my own experience as a student, my mind is constantly focused on schoolwork during the semester, which often leaves me feeling completely drained. The summer is the only time my brain can truly rest and recover. If we switched to a year-round system, students' minds would remain under constant stress without a proper recovery period, which could eventually lead to severe burnout.

Supporters of year-round schooling argue that it prevents learning loss over the summer. While this is a valid concern, there is a much simpler solution that does not require changing the entire school calendar. Schools could assign light, mandatory review homework during the summer. This would keep the previous year's material fresh in students' minds without taking away their free time. This approach offers the best of both worlds, allowing students to relax and recharge while still retaining their academic knowledge.

In conclusion, keeping the traditional summer break is a much better option than adopting a year-round school system. Changing the calendar would be unnecessary and harmful, as it would ruin summer plans and damage students' mental well-being. As the old saying goes, "If it isn't broken, don't fix it."

On September 2, 2015, a student named Generic_Name started his first year of high school. He already knew he wanted to work in medicine, but he was not sure about his specific specialty. After doing some research before high school began, he decided to become a surgeon. He took all the necessary courses, and years later, he achieved his dream, earning a good salary and living a wonderful life. In many places, students are expected to choose a career path before starting high school. Personally, I agree with this idea. Deciding on a career early allows students to find the right opportunities to prepare for their future and helps them avoid unnecessary stress.

First of all, choosing a career early gives students the chance to prepare properly for their future jobs. When you know what you want to do, you can visit different workplaces to see how professionals actually work. Additionally, you will know exactly which classes to choose in school. For example, an aspiring history teacher should focus on history classes, while a future doctor needs to take as many science courses as possible. Having a clear goal also helps you create a solid plan to achieve financial success. Therefore, identifying a career early provides the path you need to reach your professional goals.

Secondly, deciding on a career path before high school helps students avoid feeling overwhelmed and stressed. When you have a clear direction, you feel much more confident because you know what to expect. You can select the correct classes immediately, which means you will not waste time taking unnecessary courses. Furthermore, if you face any difficulties, you can easily ask teachers or counselors for guidance. Seeking help early makes the process much easier and keeps your stress levels low. Knowing your destination makes the high school journey much smoother.

On the other hand, some people believe that students should wait before choosing a career. They argue that high school is just a time for socializing with friends rather than worrying about grades, and they believe that career interests will naturally develop later, perhaps during senior year. However, waiting until the last minute makes it very difficult to choose the right college. Without a clear plan, students will likely end up feeling extremely anxious and unprepared for the future.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that students should have a career goal in mind when they enter high school. This early decision gives them the opportunity to take the right classes and prepare for their future. Most importantly, it prevents them from experiencing too much anxiety. During our school years, we are given assignments, and it is up to us to complete them. Our dedication to our work shapes our teachers' opinions of us and influences our future growth. However, there is one school practice that I strongly disagree with: teachers praising students who do not put in their best effort. In my opinion, genuine self-esteem is built on real achievements, and it is wrong to reward those who are not truly trying.

First of all, this method of boosting self-confidence makes students far too dependent on others. They start constantly looking for external validation, but in the real world, we cannot always rely on others to keep us motivated or help us succeed. Students can become overly attached to praise, expecting rewards for doing the bare minimum. If they find themselves without anyone to support or encourage them, they might stop working altogether because they lack internal motivation.

Secondly, this approach prevents students from experiencing real accomplishment. Achieving a goal brings a genuine sense of satisfaction and relief. However, if students are constantly praised just for trying, they may never actually finish their tasks because they already feel like they have succeeded. They lose the motivation to keep going, which can cause serious problems later in life. In the future, they might fail their assignments because they mistakenly believe their incomplete work is good enough.

Of course, there are some benefits when teachers encourage students, such as helping them build confidence and self-esteem, which can be useful in the future. This positive reinforcement might even inspire them to motivate others. However, teachers should not go too far by praising trivial things, like simply writing their name on a paper. Sometimes, being strict is necessary. Even if it feels difficult at first, it will benefit the students in the long run.

In conclusion, these are the reasons why I do not agree with teachers over-praising unearned efforts. Students need to learn how to work independently. While I am not saying teachers should never help, I believe their support should be focused on those who genuinely need it and are actually trying. Hopefully, we will see a change where teachers only reward real effort and dedication.

To truly develop, we must ask ourselves how we can achieve real growth. Ralph Waldo Emerson’s famous idea suggests that we cannot grow if we always do the same things, motivating us to explore unfamiliar territory.

To begin with, many professions require people to expand their horizons in order to advance. For instance, photographers who usually take still photos can improve by learning how to shoot videos, allowing them to enter the world of cinematography or journalism. They understand that exploring these new fields is the best way to develop professionally. Similarly, leaving our comfort zone is essential for personal growth. This is clear when a student decides to study abroad, or when a doctor researches new medical fields to find cures for diseases. In both cases, these individuals know that stepping into unfamiliar areas is key to their development.

Furthermore, people cannot progress if they refuse to change. For example, skilled workers like carpenters or builders might want to start their own businesses, but they are often afraid of failing at new tasks like management. To succeed, entrepreneurs must take risks, start their companies, and invest in new equipment. If they only do the same daily tasks without investing in the future, their businesses will never expand. Some might argue that repeating the same action makes someone an expert, pointing to professional athletes as an example. However, even top athletes must constantly vary their training and improve their techniques. If they never try anything new, they will not remain at the top of their game. This principle applies to any field where someone wants to be successful.

In conclusion, Ralph Waldo Emerson’s view is correct because people cannot reach their full potential if they never change their routine. To grow, we must push ourselves beyond what we are used to doing. Taking risks and trying new things will always bring benefits in the long run. Embracing change is simply a matter of willpower, and instead of mastering just one skill, we should aim to develop many.

The reduction of face-to-face human contact caused by technology has a highly negative impact on society. First, it stops the younger generation from developing essential social skills. Additionally, it facilitates online bullying and trolling.

To begin with, technology seriously damages students' social abilities. For instance, when students enter a classroom, they are constantly staring at their phones. Instead of talking to each other, they play video games on their computers. This behavior traps people in their own digital worlds, preventing them from understanding themselves and connecting with others.

Furthermore, the internet makes cyberbullying very easy. People can post hurtful videos that damage someone's self-esteem and even drive them to suicide. Others might share embarrassing photos, like someone being drunk, and tag them on Facebook or Instagram. For example, I watched a YouTube video about an Australian girl who was bullied so severely both online and at school that her family had to relocate three times.

Finally, online platforms present other dangers, such as chat rooms where users might encounter dangerous criminals like serial killers. Moreover, people use Twitter to spread fake news and rumors, such as the false claim that Michelle Obama was running for president in 2020.

In conclusion, technology limits real-world communication, hurts social development, and encourages cyberbullying and trolling. To solve this, we should turn off our phones for one or two days and spend time eating out with friends without screens. In schools, teachers should collect students' phones in a box at the classroom door to prevent use during lessons. Because online bullying has long-lasting effects, we need stricter rules, especially since technology prevents people from discussing their problems openly.

I generally disagree with the decision of some schools to offer distance learning, which allows students to attend classes from home through online platforms or video conferencing. This stance is not simply because I currently go to a public high school. Instead, I have several specific reasons why I believe this option is not a good idea for most students.

To begin with, online learning can seriously damage a student's communication skills. When you study from home, you are isolated and do not really interact with anyone other than your teacher. Personally, I think it is unhealthy for students to avoid social contact, especially if they prefer working in groups. In a physical classroom, classmates can help you understand difficult topics that you might struggle with. However, if you are studying alone at home, you miss out on this peer support.

Another major issue is that distance learning hurts student participation. In a traditional school, we do many interactive activities that help us remember the material. Asking questions in person also makes it much easier to understand difficult concepts. If you are confused during an online class, you have to send an email or message the teacher and wait for a response. This delay can be a big problem and might negatively affect your grades if you do not get help in time.

Finally, studying from home makes it very easy to become lazy and start skipping classes. If you are not a highly motivated and disciplined person, online school is extremely risky. For instance, I know this would be a disaster for me because I can be quite lazy, and I would probably miss classes by sleeping in. Of course, some very organized and responsible students can handle this responsibility and finish their education successfully, but they are the exception.

In conclusion, these are the main reasons why I do not support online classes. While distance learning can be a useful option for students who have genuine reasons for not being able to attend school physically, I believe that in-person learning remains the best choice for the majority of students.

Have you ever met someone for the first time and wondered what kind of impression you made on them? While some people believe that first impressions can be altered because everyone deserves a second chance, others argue that they are permanent because they reveal your true nature. Personally, I agree with the view that first impressions are impossible to change, as they immediately show your personality, your attitude, and who you really are.

To begin with, first impressions cannot be changed because they reflect your personality. For instance, I have a friend who wore highly inappropriate clothes to a job interview. Unsurprisingly, she did not get the position, and she struggled to find employment elsewhere for a long time after that. This experience shows that whenever we meet others, we must dress properly and speak politely. Doing so demonstrates that we are respectful, mature, and capable of taking responsibility for our actions. Ultimately, how we present ourselves initially speaks volumes about our character.

In addition, the attitude you display during a first meeting is almost impossible to erase from people's minds. I remember when I was younger, I used to be disrespectful and would argue with people who needed my help. Once, an elderly woman asked me for assistance, but I rudely refused and insulted her. She warned me that I would face a difficult life, but I ignored her. As I grew older, I tried to improve my behavior, but whenever something went wrong, people still blamed me because of my past reputation.
