When we're born, we come out of our mother's womb; the first thing we naturally do is screech and cry, and if we don't cry, the doctor hits us on our backs and tries to make us cry. And from that cry on, we develop our own kind of sound and our own screech with its own pitch. They take our fingerprints, where there will never be two of the same; even when we're born with our twin, it will never be the same, no matter how much alike we are. From there on, we start to learn and develop our own persona. After we're born, our brain starts to function even with little stuff; babies learn to cry when they're hungry, want to be changed, when they're in pain, or simply want attention. When children get older, into the toddler stage, they start to learn how to walk by observing everyone else; they learn to talk by listening to everyone else around them. We learn how to grab our bottle, pick up a fork or spoon, and, practically, our own daily doings. But we learn all that from observing and listening to everyone else. When we hit our 6–12 years of age, where we have a tendency that we want to fit in, be in the cool kids' group, and we watch TV, see celebrities, see that there are musicians, actors, painters, policemen, firemen, dentists, doctors, mayors, chefs, soccer players, basketball players, football players, baseball players, hockey players, tennis players, volleyball players, etc.—the list could go on and on—but the point here is the fact that we are influenced. But as we get older, in our teen years, 13–19, we start to have our own kind of voice, at least until we're old enough to make them. We all take our own paths, and we choose to make the decisions that we make; our parents don't go with us throughout the day telling us what to do or not do, making our each and every decision for us. They sure do give us a hell of a lot of advice because they already went through that stage and they don't want to see us fail and get hurt, but sometimes it's good that we fail and make mistakes because then we learn what we can or cannot do. Now, as you turn into an adult, that net that we used to have when we were living under Mom and Dad's roof is no longer there; it's gone. We don't have that privilege anymore, and we need to grow up and create and develop our own persona officially. When you get a job, it comes with responsibilities, and from there we learn if we're responsible or irresponsible, if we're social or non-social, if we're lenient or non-lenient, patient or impatient, forgiving or unforgiving. I'd like to think that we're all born to grow and learn about our rugged society, and based on what we've lived is how we're going to act, because we can literally live in a shithole of a place and have the happiest attitude ever, and have a better attitude than a boy or girl complaining that she didn't get the car she wanted, versus the kid that saw his mother get beat by his deadbeat dad, or the kid that was up all night wondering if his mom was going to come home tonight, or even the kid that went to sleep hungry. So honestly, I don't think that we're born with labels; I feel like we all can make our own decisions of what we're going to make of life, if you're going to sit there and make everyone see you as a pity. A huge play of your character is your mentality; if you have a broken-down, weak mindset, you're going to have negative vibes and a weak, deadbeat character, but if you have a strong mindset and the will to get stuff done, then you'll have a broad and respected character. In conclusion, I'd like to think that we create and build our own character, and that we're not given a label by any higher power of what our character is going to be in life.

When we are born, our very first action is to cry. If we do not make a sound immediately, the doctor gently taps us to encourage that first breath. From that moment on, we develop our own unique voice and pitch. Even identical twins, who look exactly alike, have completely different fingerprints. This shows that we are unique from the very beginning, and from this point, we start to build our own individual personality.

As babies, our brains quickly begin to process information. We learn to cry to communicate our basic needs, such as hunger, discomfort, or the desire for attention. As we grow into toddlers, we learn to walk and talk by watching and listening to the people around us. We figure out how to hold a bottle or use a spoon simply by observing others. Almost all of our early daily habits are learned through this imitation of our environment.

Between the ages of six and twelve, we experience a strong desire to fit in and belong to the popular groups. During this stage, we are highly influenced by the world around us. We watch television and see celebrities, athletes, musicians, and professionals like doctors, firefighters, and chefs. These figures serve as role models and shape our early interests and aspirations.

As we enter our teenage years, we begin to find our own voice and make our own choices. Our parents no longer guide our every move or make decisions for us throughout the day. Although they offer valuable advice based on their own life experiences to protect us from harm, making mistakes is a crucial part of growing up. Failing allows us to learn our limits and understand what we can and cannot do.

When we finally become adults, the safety net provided by our parents disappears. We must grow up and officially establish our own identity. Entering the workforce brings new responsibilities. Through our jobs, we discover our true traits—whether we are responsible or careless, social or reserved, patient or impatient, and forgiving or resentful. 

Ultimately, we are all born to grow and navigate a challenging world. Our character is not determined by our circumstances, but by how we react to them. For instance, a person raised in a very difficult and impoverished environment can still maintain a positive and happy attitude. In contrast, someone raised in privilege might constantly complain about minor issues. Our mindset plays a major role in who we become. A weak and negative mindset leads to a weak character, whereas a strong mindset and determination build a respected and resilient personality.

In conclusion, we are not born with pre-determined labels or destinies created by a higher power. Instead, we have the freedom to make our own choices, build our own character, and decide what we want to make of our lives.

Imagine being forced to participate in a school activity. If a principal makes this mandatory for everyone, it can cause problems because some students need to rest, while others simply dislike sports or organized events. Furthermore, young people need free time to relax and choose their own hobbies.

Students need to rest because they already work hard in class and require energy to function. Relaxation actually helps them regain the strength they need for daily life. Additionally, teenagers enjoy socializing and chatting with their peers. During structured activities, they cannot easily talk to each other. Hanging out and talking is a form of relaxation because they do not have to run around; they can just enjoy each other's company. Resting is essential for children to keep their energy levels up for other important tasks.

Many students prefer indoor hobbies over physical activities. For example, they might enjoy playing video games with their friends, which is very fun for them. Some children simply do not like going outdoors and prefer staying inside to read, play, or relax. They might not be interested in sports, or they might feel uncomfortable because they do not have close friends to participate with in these group activities. Ultimately, many kids prefer to do their own thing rather than forced school programs.

In conclusion, forcing students to join school activities is not a good policy. Students need downtime, and some just do not enjoy these events. If I were the principal, I would allow students to choose how they spend their time. If they want to stay indoors or rest because they are tired, that should be fine, and if they want to join a club, they should have that option too.

What exactly is self-reliance? Simply put, it is the ability of students and adults to make independent decisions for themselves and their communities. Today, we face many complex challenges that affect the entire United States, such as government shutdowns that harm local businesses, farms, and everyday citizens. To solve these issues, seeking guidance and help is absolutely essential. We cannot rely on just one person's perspective; instead, we need to collaborate, speak up, and share diverse ideas to find the best solutions. By teaching these skills to our children, we help them become strong leaders rather than mere followers. True leaders might start small, but they constantly ask questions and gather information to build their knowledge over time.

These skills are highly relevant to our families, careers, and daily lifestyles. Self-reliance is not just for students; seeking advice and learning from others makes us much better professionals and individuals. While we are learning, we are also teaching others around us. Self-reliance is closely linked to leadership, which means standing up for your career and what you believe is right. We all want to be correct, but we must not fear being wrong. By asking questions and listening to other people's opinions, we gain more options and perspectives to consider. This collaborative mindset is necessary even for global decisions that impact us all.

Consider the military, where soldiers hold the lives of others in their hands. Service members have to make incredibly difficult choices on the battlefield. To prepare them, basic training focuses on developing their minds and self-reliance skills so they can make quick decisions when commanders are not immediately available. However, even in these high-pressure situations, asking questions and getting feedback is critical. It helps soldiers understand their environment and resources. This lesson applies to civilian life too, whether we are making major decisions about our careers or our children.

Regardless of our age, race, gender, or background, developing these decision-making skills is vital for both the present and the future. We want to pass these lessons about finance and business down to our children. At the same time, we must stay informed about our government to prevent economic disasters like stock market crashes. We need to use our voices and skills to support our communities. Our society needs active citizens to help the country thrive, protecting our homes and employment.

Ultimately, our jobs and businesses are connected to the stability of the government. A government shutdown can lead to financial ruin, causing people to lose their livelihoods and homes. Instead of focusing on superficial desires, like buying a brand-new car, we should focus on guiding one another and sharing innovative ideas. We should never be afraid to ask questions, as learning is a lifelong process. No one is perfect, and we will continue to learn until we are old. I encourage everyone to keep seeking guidance, sharing ideas, and never stop asking questions.

Summer is a special time meant for enjoying the warm weather, spending time with family and friends, and playing with pets. During these months, no student wants to worry about school assignments or struggle to complete homework. In my opinion, after a long and demanding academic year, students truly need a proper period to relax and recharge.

This need for a significant break is not just for young people; we can see a similar situation with adults. Working adults also require long vacations because they get exhausted and stressed by their jobs. While I am not saying students and adults have the exact same lives—since adults obviously have much heavier responsibilities—students still need understanding. They need to recover their energy and get enough sleep. Unfortunately, many jobs only offer a week or two of vacation, leaving adults feeling constantly tired. This is why they often wish for longer breaks to spend time with their families. Since students actually have the opportunity to enjoy a long vacation, they should definitely take advantage of it.

Furthermore, most students love summer because of the warm breeze, the sunny weather, and the wonderful feeling of freedom. Knowing that you do not have to worry about grades, projects, or exams makes a huge difference, and this feeling cannot be replaced by shorter breaks throughout the year. Of course, I understand the perspective of educators. Teachers do not like having to repeat lessons at the beginning of the year because students forgot what they learned, which can be very frustrating. However, everyone loves a long vacation, and many teachers also benefit from this time off by saving money to enjoy their summer.

From a student's point of view, I completely agree with the need for a long break to rest. However, there is another important reason why summer vacation should remain long. Many students use this time to achieve personal goals, such as getting a full-time summer job. Even some teachers do this. Working during the summer allows students to save money for their daily needs or, more importantly, for college. This is especially crucial for students who do not have financial support from their families and must rely on themselves to fund their education.

I understand that some educators suggest a different schedule, such as a three-to-four-week summer break combined with longer winter, spring, and fall breaks. While this sounds nice because some people love autumn or winter weather, it would ultimately make the summer break much shorter. In conclusion, our current long summer break is perfect. The weather is beautiful, the beaches are open, and there is plenty of time to travel and visit family. It also gives students a valuable opportunity to work, earn extra money, and cover their expenses. Therefore, we should keep the summer break just the way it is.

In many ways, I believe technology has both positive and negative effects on our lives. Whether these changes are good or bad mostly depends on the individual using them.

On the positive side, technology can be a great help for people who feel lonely. Feeling completely alone is one of the worst experiences, and it can really damage a person's mental state. In fact, some people would prefer other difficult situations, like being unemployed, rather than facing extreme loneliness. For these individuals, technology offers a wonderful escape. They can read books, shop online, play video games, listen to music on apps like Pandora, or watch their favorite shows on YouTube and Netflix. Using devices this way is a very positive aspect of modern life.

However, nothing in this world is perfect. As my grandfather used to say, bad things must exist so that we can appreciate the good things. Every advantage usually comes with a disadvantage.

The negative side is that because of smartphones and other devices, people are losing interest in normal social activities. For example, many do not care about family gatherings anymore. Personally, I never enjoyed formal family reunions much either, as I preferred hanging out with my cousins and childhood friends instead of listening to boring adult conversations. However, nowadays, it is difficult to have even a simple conversation with someone. While you are talking, they are often staring at their screens. To me, this is very disrespectful because it shows they do not care about what you are saying, which can easily damage relationships.

Undeniably, technology is one of the greatest inventions in history. It makes communication effortless, provides endless entertainment, and keeps us informed about world events and even space exploration. We no longer need to search through heavy books to find answers. Everything has become much easier; we can shop or order food without ever leaving the house. Yet, this convenience can make people lazy. People might start wondering why they should do anything when a phone or computer can do it for them. They might ask why they should go on real dates or talk to people in person when they can just do it online. If people keep thinking this way, they might eventually find themselves completely alone in the future.

In conclusion, technology is an excellent tool, but only if we use it when necessary and do not let it control our minds and lives.

Technology is an excellent tool in our daily lives because it assists us in many different ways, such as with tasks, communication, and entertainment. Today, technology is advancing very rapidly in our society. Through devices like smartphones, tablets, and computers, we can easily access global news or connect with our parents, friends, and classmates with just a few clicks.

There are many positive effects of technology in our society. It helps us with shopping, entertainment, and accessing useful applications. For instance, we can use free tools like translation apps, digital books, and GPS. One major reason technology is so important in our daily lives is the help it provides when we are lost. If someone is in an unfamiliar place, they can use the GPS on their phone to find their destination, a store, or a supermarket. This makes technology an incredibly valuable tool for handling unexpected situations.

Another benefit is the entertainment that technology offers when we are bored. If you do not know what to do, you can listen to music from any artist or genre in the world. Additionally, technology makes it very easy to download games and books. Finding a book on a phone or tablet is much simpler than going to a physical bookstore; you only need to type the title, and your device will show you various options. The internet also offers thousands of games for everyone, including sports, adventures, and puzzles.

Furthermore, technology is a wonderful way to communicate, regardless of the distance between people. Applications like Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger are very user-friendly, allowing anyone to use them without difficulty. These platforms give us the opportunity to feel closer to our families and childhood friends by letting us see their photos and videos. Therefore, technology is a great treasure that we should use wisely to avoid problems in our lives.

In addition, technology helps us find solutions to everyday problems, such as cooking a new meal or repairing things around the house or car. We can easily find step-by-step video tutorials on websites like Google and YouTube. These videos show us tips and instructions so we can learn how to fix things ourselves. At the same time, these platforms can also help us find professional mechanics or other experts who can assist us with more complex issues.

Technology also helps people find employment in their desired fields. For example, if someone wants a job at a company, they can easily complete an online application. This process is very convenient because almost everyone has internet access through their phones, computers, or tablets. From a business perspective, companies use technology to advertise their products and quality to a wider audience. By using the internet, a local business can quickly become an international company and increase its profits, as the internet is the easiest way for customers to see what they offer.

In conclusion, technology is an amazing tool for human life. It helps us communicate, find entertainment, search for jobs, and solve daily problems like repairs or navigation. My uncle once had one hundred dollars in his wallet. He gave me ten dollars and kept the rest. I advised him to save his money because he would need it the next day, but he ignored me and spent everything on a new shirt, pants, and hats. Consequently, the very next day, he had to ask around for gas money for his car. When our friend heard our opinions, he saw the situation from a different perspective. Even though he initially wanted the cinema experience, he realized it was a waste of money and decided to follow our advice.

Instead of buying the shirt, I obsessively spent the money on a video game. The next day, I had to beg my dad for more money to buy the shirt. He reminded me that he had warned me, but I simply had not listened. Since that day, I have learned to listen to advice and save my money for these types of situations.

In conclusion, these experiences show how important it is to listen to the people around us. Many problems happen because we ignore good advice. Sometimes, hearing different perspectives from more than one person is exactly what we need to make the right decision.

I completely agree with this idea because achieving a successful life requires learning how to make things easier for yourself. You can do this by showing the world that you are a special, kind person, regardless of what others say or think about you. When problems arise, it is essential to face them calmly and with a positive attitude, because getting angry never helps solve anything in a constructive way. For this reason, you should treat everyone well, maintain peace in your soul, and, most importantly, build strong connections with the people around you. Facing everything that comes your way with a smile is the key to a better life.

When you treat others with kindness, you make them feel good, and you also feel better about yourself. Being a nice person shows that you are different from the crowd. Although there are many negative people in the world, this should not stop you from being kind. The best approach is simply to distance yourself from those with bad attitudes and find people who share your values. Surrounding yourself with positive people will make you feel like you are part of a family, and they will support you on your path to success. For example, I always try to be a good person to my family and friends. My friends are very special to me, and we share a strong bond because I took the time to truly understand them, their interests, and how they like to spend their time. Because they see me as a successful person, it motivates me to keep a positive attitude around them. I want them in my life, and I am sure they will also have successful futures because of their great qualities.

Having inner peace is another crucial part of a happy life because it brings positive emotions from deep within your soul, making you feel comfortable. Of course, we all face uncomfortable situations sometimes, but we must still strive to find our inner peace. I know this can be very difficult. Lacking peace inside can negatively affect many areas of your life. To achieve this peace, you should focus on doing activities you truly enjoy and try not to get angry easily. Getting upset over a single problem can ruin your entire weekend, which is not healthy. I remember when I was twelve years old, my younger brother did something that really upset me. Even though I am twenty now, that memory still stays with me, and holding onto those negative thoughts is not good. However, whenever I remember it, I remind myself how much I love my brother and how close we are. He is always there to listen to me, and talking to him about my life brings peace back to my soul.

Building good connections with the people around you can also help you maintain a positive attitude. If you spend time with optimistic people who talk about useful things, they will have a positive influence on your future because they know what they want in life. These are the kinds of interesting people you can learn from and share ideas with. Throughout your life, you will meet many different people. Some might seem very fun and constantly invite you to go out and party, making you think they are the right friends for a successful life. However, the best people are often those who offer you support and advice that will benefit your future, rather than just inviting you to parties. Sometimes we mistake helpful people for being boring or bad, but that is a mistake. For instance, I knew a student in the seventh grade who had a very bright future. He always got excellent grades, did his homework, and was very polite. However, in the ninth grade, he started hanging out with classmates who did not care about school or their futures. Soon, his grades dropped because he was always doing negative things with his new friends. In the end, I believe he did not even go to college. This shows how important it is to surround yourself with people who will help you succeed.

In conclusion, these three main points—being a kind person to everyone, maintaining inner peace, and building positive connections with others—clearly show how vital a good attitude is. Showing kindness and staying positive, no matter what challenges you face in life, is the ultimate key to a happy and successful future.

Technology has a significant impact on our lives, bringing both positive and negative consequences, especially regarding how it limits human contact. Today, technology is present almost everywhere. Without it, we would miss many opportunities to learn new things. Furthermore, people no longer need to meet face-to-face to have a conversation. Because of advanced technology, anyone with a phone can text someone living in another country or continent. Technology simply makes our lives much easier, and I believe its overall influence is highly positive. Here are some examples to support this view.

First of all, technology is used in many areas of daily life, creating many positive outcomes. For instance, many people rely on technology for their jobs. If they have a question, they can find the answer immediately online without needing to ask anyone else, which allows them to work and earn a living. In schools, both teachers and students depend heavily on technology. Students often complete their assignments on computers and submit them via the internet. In the United States, for example, schools use technology for about half of their work to find information instead of using traditional books. Another group that relies heavily on technology is medical doctors. They use advanced medical devices to perform complex surgeries, which helps them save more lives than in the past. Today, doctors trust these technological tools more than old medical books. Additionally, factories use automated machinery to do heavy labor, such as packing products, which reduces the physical strain on human workers.

On the other hand, humans can choose to use technology for either good or bad purposes. Over time, people have gradually learned how to use these tools. Most people use technology for positive reasons, such as in their professions. Secretaries, teachers, and doctors use it to communicate and store important data. Parents also use technology to educate and entertain their children. In Latin American countries, some parents even refer to smartphones and tablets as the "new babysitter" because these devices are an easy way to keep children distracted when mothers need to get chores done, without needing to hire someone else. However, some people use technology for harmful activities. They learn how to use digital platforms to commit fraud or stalk others on social media. Sometimes, criminals use these tools to kidnap people or steal money from bank accounts. There are many cases where older criminals try to deceive children through social media or online video games. In some tragic cases, this leads to death. Another negative aspect is hacking, where individuals steal bank accounts and personal information using sophisticated software. This shows that when people are given access to technology, not everyone will use it in a good way.

Furthermore, technology changes how people live and think. For example, it makes people feel safer in their homes because of advanced security systems. It also allows creative people to build careers on social media, such as YouTubers who share their passions with an audience they cannot see, yet they talk to them as if they know them. Technology has also changed how older generations think. In the past, they had to write paper letters, but now they can easily send text messages or make video calls instead of meeting in person. In this sense, limiting physical contact is acceptable because you can still connect with others. For instance, if you are playing an online game with a friend who lives on the other side of the world, you cannot talk face-to-face, but technology allows you to communicate and play together, which is a positive aspect of this limitation.

In conclusion, limiting human contact can sometimes have negative effects. In the workplace, it is important to communicate directly with your colleagues to maintain a good working relationship. Similarly, in a romantic relationship, you cannot rely only on text messages; partners need to talk in person to build a strong connection. On the other hand, technology is very helpful in school when you need to find information and verify what your classmates say. However, because some people are lazy and do not want to read books, they rely too much on the internet, even though technology does not always provide the correct answers. Ultimately, while both face-to-face and digital communication have their advantages and disadvantages, I believe we still need more real human interaction than technological communication in our lives.

In some societies, young people are expected to choose their future career by the time they start high school. Some believe this early decision is beneficial because it helps students prepare for college, secure a job afterwards, and avoid future stress. However, forcing teenagers to choose a career path so early can be a mistake. It often leads to students quitting their classes, causes excessive stress and overthinking, and ultimately results in a waste of time.

First of all, many students who choose a career path too early end up abandoning their courses. For example, after attending a specialized class for just a few weeks, they often give up because they lose interest or find the workload too difficult to manage. This struggle shows that teenagers need to think carefully and be sure of their interests before committing to specific career-focused classes.

Additionally, deciding on a career requires a significant amount of mental effort that young people might not be ready for. Even adults take a long time to establish their careers. Most adults focus on finding any job first to earn money and enjoy their social lives with friends, only building their actual career once they are financially stable. Expecting young students to make these complex decisions is unrealistic.

Finally, forcing this choice on children is often a waste of time because they are not mature enough. At a young age, kids prefer playing video games and enjoying their hobbies rather than planning their professional future, which they simply view as extra schoolwork. When asked to choose a career, many will simply write "I don't know" and return to their play. Therefore, proper guidance and planning are necessary before making such big decisions.

In conclusion, pressuring children aged twelve or younger to choose a career is a careless approach. It causes them to overthink, lose motivation, and quickly give up on their studies after only a few weeks. Instead of forcing kids to write "I don't know" on career forms, we must understand that building a career takes time, and young people should not be rushed into decisions they cannot yet handle.

Although some people believe the opposite, starting with modest goals is highly beneficial because it allows you to identify and correct minor mistakes early on. By setting lower initial targets, individuals can focus on reviewing and fixing these small errors. Ultimately, addressing these minor issues is what builds your strength and prepares you for much greater challenges in the future.

Often, the people who begin at the very bottom are the ones who end up exceeding their own expectations. By setting realistic, lower goals and achieving them one by one, they build a solid foundation. The mistakes they make along the way are not failures; instead, they help build character, making these individuals more resilient and capable of handling whatever comes their way.

On the other hand, some people aim too high right from the start, foolishly believing they can reach the top without facing any obstacles or putting in real effort. However, this approach often leads to failure. It is much better to start a bit lower so you can gradually develop the skills and character needed to reach your goals. For instance, someone who tries to achieve too much at once risks losing everything with a single careless step because they did not stop to think. By starting small, you avoid unnecessary risks and can learn valuable lessons at every stage of the journey.

Setting low-risk goals also prevents you from losing what you have already worked so hard to achieve. Progressing step-by-step allows you to analyze your current situation and make steady improvements. While it is good to challenge yourself occasionally, you should never do so at the risk of losing everything you have built. Dear City Council,

I believe that implementing a curfew for teenagers is a great idea because it will keep them out of trouble. Some teenagers stay out late just to cause problems for others. Having a 10 p.m. curfew makes sense because many teens hang around on the streets, playing loud music and disturbing the peace. At the same time, other students are trying to study and sleep so they can do well in school. If the council adopts this curfew, there should be a law stating that teenagers on the streets after 10 p.m. are breaking the rules.

Many young people end up in jail because they get involved in dangerous activities. Some teenagers carry guns, even though they are under 18 and cannot legally own them. Sometimes, innocent teens go to jail simply because they were hanging out with others who had weapons. Furthermore, teenagers often find discarded guns in places like rivers. When they pick them up, they get blamed for whatever crimes were previously committed with those weapons. A curfew would protect these teenagers and help them avoid these dangerous situations.

Some people argue that a curfew interferes too much with the lives of young people. While it is true that a curfew limits their freedom, it is necessary because some teenagers make poor choices when left unsupervised. The curfew is not meant to punish them, but rather to guide and protect them.

In conclusion, I strongly support the 10 p.m. curfew. It is a practical way to keep teenagers safe, prevent them from getting into trouble, and ensure they have a better future.

Therefore, we must always keep working hard and stay consistent in everything we do.

The famous writer Ralph Waldo Emerson once stated that people cannot grow unless they attempt tasks that go beyond what they have already mastered, and this is completely true. To fully grasp this idea, we must realize that mastering a skill means being able to perform it perfectly every time. Personal growth requires us to set new targets. Even if we only take small steps at first, these actions guide us toward achieving much greater things. Although mastering a new skill can take years of hard work, having self-confidence and belief in yourself will eventually lead to success.

For instance, if you already know how to ride a bicycle, you should challenge yourself to ride a motorcycle. If you can bake a simple cupcake, try making a whole cake, or if you can float in water, teach yourself how to swim. Taking on these slightly harder tasks helps you build on the skills you already possess. By upgrading these abilities, you can reach higher levels and accomplish bigger goals. You will never achieve your dreams unless you push your limits, which requires dedication and continuous effort. Even if you fail at a small task initially, you must keep trying until you succeed. Ultimately, the choice is yours: you can either challenge yourself to grow as an individual, or stay in your comfort zone and never reach your full potential.

I believe that when people receive a first impression, their reactions and ability to change vary greatly. Everyone has a unique attitude, meaning no two people will respond in the exact same way. Sometimes, individuals do not change at all because they simply do not care about the feedback. On the other hand, some people do alter their behavior, and this reaction is usually based on the personal experiences they have already gone through in their lives.

Many people ignore their first impressions because they are indifferent, continuing their daily routines without caring about what others say about them. However, when they receive a genuinely bad impression, it can act as a wake-up call. They begin to analyze their actions and reflect on what they did wrong. Real personal growth only happens when a person truly feels the need to transform who they are. This process takes time, and people often struggle to change quickly because they might repeat the same mistakes without thinking.

This dynamic is also very visible in romantic relationships, where issues like jealousy, toxicity, and bad influences often arise. For instance, many adolescents suffer deeply, sometimes with tragic consequences, when they get the impression that their partner is betraying them with someone else. People often do not realize how devastating dishonesty can be to a partner in that moment. Relationships should not be about making others jealous or trying to impress people; instead, being willing to change is a positive way to build a healthy connection.

In my own experience, I used to believe that changing my personality was completely impossible. At one point, I was told that my attitude was disappointing to those around me. This feedback made me feel extremely discouraged, and I started thinking negatively every day, believing I could never be good at the things others excelled at. It was hard to change because my behavior felt comfortable to me, even if it was bad for others. Eventually, I decided that I had to change who I was, no matter how difficult it would be, and I knew I could do it with or without help.

Ultimately, I believe that first impressions can motivate us to change. Changing is a great way to show everyone that we are not the same person we used to be, and every impression we receive serves as a lesson to help us avoid repeating the same mistakes in the future. Although people might say it is impossible to forget our past actions, making a daily effort helps us get better at moving forward. None of us are perfect, but we can always improve our attitudes and learn to be more careful about who we trust.

I strongly believe that students would benefit greatly from having the option to attend classes from home. This approach allows them to be more prepared for their lessons and helps them maintain a much higher level of focus.

One of the main reasons for this is the social pressure found in traditional schools. Sometimes, students feel too embarrassed to show their true potential because they are intimidated by classmates who seem smarter or speak English better. This can make them feel like they cannot succeed. However, we can still achieve our goals without physically going to school. For instance, when a student is studying alone at home, they do not have anyone constantly telling them what to do. If they have questions during an online class, they are forced to find solutions on their own first. This builds independence. Of course, if they still need help, they can easily text their teacher for assistance.

In addition, studying from home offers incredible comfort and flexibility. If a student gets hungry after working hard all morning, they can quickly go to the kitchen, make a snack, and return to their room to continue their homework. This pressure-free environment is perfect for shy students who might need a more personalized explanation from their teacher. It also benefits those who struggle to wake up early, as they can choose to study later in the day or even at night. Furthermore, this flexibility is extremely helpful for pregnant students and young mothers. I remember a friend of mine who went through a very difficult time during her pregnancy. She had to walk around school looking exhausted, and after giving birth, she tried to continue her classes at home. It was very stressful for her when the baby cried or needed to be fed while a teacher was there, and she hated leaving her baby to go back to school. If she had been able to take all her classes online, it would have been much easier for her.

Of course, there are challenges, such as families who might not have the money or resources for online learning. However, online classes actually make it easier for students who need to work to support themselves. Instead of missing school because they are tired or distracted, students can balance both responsibilities. They can work for a few hours and then study at home, or work one day and study the next. This flexibility makes it much easier to pass classes and exams. Ultimately, if we want to succeed, we must never give up. By researching information, trying to solve problems, and studying hard, we can prove our doubters wrong.

Online learning also offers great academic tools, such as video conferences that clearly explain difficult subjects like math. There are many specific advantages to studying from home, including:
- Spending more time using the computer for learning.
- Having a stronger focus on homework.
- Using smartphones to look up information whenever necessary.
- Being able to study throughout the day.
- Avoiding distractions from talking to friends during class.
- Finishing assignments much faster.

Finally, staying at home protects students from many outside problems. During the winter, they do not have to worry about the freezing weather or choosing the right clothes. They also do not have to deal with school drama, peer conflicts, or seeing people who put them in a bad mood. Many students suffer from depression, and being forced into a stressful school environment can make it worse. Allowing these students to take classes from home is much better for their mental health and overall well-being.

A highly debated topic is whether students should choose their future careers when they start high school and select courses based on that choice. In my opinion, forcing young students to commit to a career path so early is a bad idea. Teenagers are simply not mature enough to make such major life decisions, and they often lack the seriousness required for these choices.

To begin with, high school freshmen are too young to know exactly what they want to do for the rest of their lives. They have no real-world work experience and do not understand how different careers function. It is much better to wait until junior or senior year to explore various career options. This allows students to choose the right courses later on, when they are more prepared and have a better understanding of their interests.

Another reason is that teenagers frequently change their minds or want to try new things. If a student is forced to choose a path in their freshman year and later decides to change it, all the specialized classes they took will be wasted, and they will have to start over with new courses. For instance, a friend of mine chose a technology class in his first year. However, after researching the average salary, he realized it was not what he wanted. He ended up switching to a materials and processes class to learn how to build houses instead.

Furthermore, young people are prone to making wrong decisions because of their lack of maturity. Instead of rushing into a career path, the best approach during the early years of high school is to focus on general education, take a variety of good classes, and learn how to be responsible.

In conclusion, students should focus on getting good grades and doing well in high school first. By the time they reach their senior year or enter college, they will have more life experience and a clearer understanding of the world. This is the ideal time to select specific courses that will successfully guide them toward their chosen career.

Author Ralph Waldo Emerson wrote "Unless you try to do something beyond what you have already mastered, you will never grow." This is a true fact, and you should try to be a better human or person in life and become someone that people can look up too.

I strongly agree with Ralph Waldo Emerson’s statement that we cannot grow unless we attempt things beyond our current abilities. In my seventeen years of life, I have realized that staying inside your comfort zone prevents you from achieving anything meaningful. If you always choose the easy path, you will never push yourself to become the best version of who you can be.

Remaining comfortable might feel safe, but it is actually a waste of time and energy. Instead of settling, we should use our time to develop into better individuals who can share knowledge and positive experiences with others. We must constantly strive to reach our full potential.

Improving yourself is always the right choice. Pushing your limits allows you to gain more education, which can lead to better career opportunities and higher pay. More importantly, having greater knowledge enables you to assist people who cannot help themselves. As human beings, we should support one another, even offering help to those who are too proud to ask for it.

Some people might disagree because they are selfish or believe they have already reached their peak. They think they have mastered everything and have nothing left to learn. However, they are mistaken. Humans can always learn something new and become better parents, children, and citizens. We should never settle for just being "okay" when we can do more.

We must learn to step out of our cozy routines and try to improve a little bit every single day. Learning new things and communicating with others will only benefit us. Ultimately, Emerson's quote is absolutely true. By constantly challenging ourselves, we can grow into better people and become positive role models for others to look up to.

Have you ever spotted something valuable on the ground, picked it up, and acted as if it belonged to you? This action is actually a form of dishonesty. It is a bad habit because you do not know who the item belongs to. When the rightful owner eventually returns to search for their lost money or toy, it is already gone because someone else decided to walk away with it. When I was a child, I frequently witnessed people dropping their belongings. Instead of keeping them, I would always return the items immediately or call out to let them know they had dropped something. Unfortunately, when most people see a lost object lying around, their very first instinct is to claim it for themselves. However, this is not a smart decision because taking something that does not belong to you is simply stealing.

Many people advise leaving lost items exactly where they are because the owners will likely return to look for them. After all, nobody loses their belongings on purpose without caring about them. Many schools emphasize this important lesson. In my elementary school, there were posters everywhere reminding us to leave lost things where they were and not to take what was not ours. While many students followed these rules, some people simply do not care, which is unfair because they usually do not even need the item; they just want it. There is a big difference between needing and wanting. Needing something means it is essential for your life, and losing it causes a real struggle. If you truly need an item, you can usually purchase it from a local store. On the other hand, wanting something means you do not actually require it, but you desire it to show off, have fun, or simply because you feel like taking it, even though you can easily afford it and are not facing any difficulties.

To avoid these selfish behaviors, we should follow a few simple guidelines:

- If you find an item, do not keep it.
- If you see someone drop something, return it immediately.
- Always be conscious of your actions.
- Do not give in to peer pressure.
- Try to be helpful.
- Be kind to others.

This lesson is incredibly important today because many people ignore these values, and some parents no longer teach them to their children. Consequently, schools must step in to educate young kids about right and wrong. When you see someone drop an item, you should always hand it back. Think about how you would feel if you lost your favorite toy—something you saved up for and cherished—and someone else just walked away with it. You would probably feel angry, sad, and deeply upset because your favorite possession is gone forever, taken by someone who did not care about your feelings and just wanted it for themselves. Now, imagine the opposite scenario. You drop your favorite toy, and a kind stranger notices, runs up to you, and returns it. You would feel incredibly happy and relieved. That person had no intention of keeping it because they knew they were not the rightful owner, and they wanted to do the right thing before you walked away and realized it was gone.

I experienced this firsthand when I lost my iPad years ago. Someone found it and kept it without a second thought. I was devastated and had to share my mother's phone for a long time until my father could buy me a replacement. This is why we must teach children that keeping lost property is wrong. People who steal often only realize the pain of theft when they become victims themselves, wondering why it happened to them, not realizing it is a consequence of their own past actions.

Furthermore, many modern items are extremely expensive. For instance, people are highly attached to their smartphones. If someone cracks their screen, they get frustrated because it affects how the device functions. Losing a phone entirely is much worse, especially since new models can cost over a thousand dollars, which is almost as much as a cheap used car. People rely on their phones for critical tasks, such as calling for a ride or contacting emergency services. If someone stole my phone, I would be furious and miserable because replacing such an expensive item is very difficult. Therefore, we must always choose to be honest and return what we find.

Can you truly achieve greatness in this world simply by being yourself? I strongly believe that if you always stay true to yourself and maintain self-belief, you can accomplish anything. Because he believed in his mission and had immense faith, he remained positive and dedicated to his dream. He truly believed he could make this vision a reality. After years of persistent effort, he finally achieved his goal, famously delivering his speech in Washington, D.C. His story proves that if you have a dream and work constantly to achieve it, you can succeed just by being true to yourself.

However, Ronaldo never planned to give up because he had a deep passion for soccer and believed in his own potential. At just thirteen years old, he worked in the mornings and practiced soccer in the afternoons. He quickly became the best player in his area, joined his country's youth setup by age fifteen, and eventually became a world-famous soccer star. His journey shows that when you believe in yourself, no obstacle can stop you from reaching your goals.

Even when you doubt your abilities, you can succeed if you keep trying and maintain your self-belief. With faith and confidence, everything becomes possible. Once you start working toward a goal, never give up and keep trusting yourself. You can turn your imagination and aspirations into reality simply by staying true to who you are. If you have a dream or a passion, start believing in yourself today.

Because they fear being teased by their peers, these students often keep their medical conditions secret. Since schools do not have complete information about every student's dietary restrictions, changing the ingredients on the menu could be highly dangerous.

Although some schools have the budget to afford new things, changing the lunch menu to make students happier often backfires. Administrators do not realize how picky students can be. When kids reject the new meals and throw them away, the school wastes a significant amount of money. This financial loss is not worth it. If students do not appreciate the new food options, schools should spend that budget on other resources that students would actually enjoy.

In conclusion, schools should keep the lunch menus exactly as they are. Attempting to change them leads to wasted money, untouched food, and potential health risks for students with undisclosed allergies. To avoid these issues, schools should avoid making any changes. Keeping the current menu saves money, keeps students satisfied, and ensures that everyone stays safe and healthy.

Have you ever wondered why some students graduate at such a young age? Is it simply because they are smarter than their classmates? While some people might argue that finishing high school in three years is a bad idea, it is actually a very positive choice. Graduating early helps teenagers become mature enough for the real world and teaches them to take full responsibility for their own lives.

First of all, graduating in three years is beneficial because it prepares young people for the realities of life. Many teenagers today do not understand how the real world actually functions. For instance, some teens engage in dangerous behaviors like drinking and driving, causing accidents that hurt themselves and others. Because their parents always rescue them from trouble, they never learn to think about the consequences of their actions. Furthermore, when parents constantly defend their children's mistakes or protect them after they break the law, these teenagers believe they did nothing wrong. Consequently, they cannot learn from their errors. Graduating early forces teenagers to grow up, understand their environment, and take responsibility for their own actions.

Secondly, finishing school early encourages teenagers to become financially independent. In the real world, adults must pay for their own rent, electricity, and phone bills. Currently, many teenagers do not care about where money comes from because their parents cover all these expenses. For example, my mother pays for my phone bill, so I do not worry about the cost. Similarly, many teens waste water and electricity without thinking because they do not have to pay the bills themselves. If teenagers graduate early and start supporting themselves, they will quickly learn the value of money and become much more careful with their utility consumption.

On the other hand, some people argue that graduating in three years is a mistake. They believe that early graduates miss out on the fun of teenage life, experience too much stress, and do not have time to enjoy the moment. However, the benefits of entering adulthood early far outweigh these concerns because it prepares you for future success.

In conclusion, graduating in three years is an excellent path for young people. It helps them mature faster, teaches them to take full responsibility for their actions, and prepares them to manage their own finances. Ultimately, this choice gives teenagers a head start in understanding what life has in store for them.

The famous president Thomas Jefferson once wrote, "It is wonderful how much may be done if we are always doing." This quote suggests that constant effort, whether for ourselves or for our community, leads to great achievements. While some people believe that inactivity is necessary to rest and regain strength, others argue that staying active is far better because hard work helps us reach our goals and contribute to society.

Every day, millions of people wake up and do their best at work. However, even those who do not have a job can still find ways to be active and contribute to their own personal growth or to society. For example, one can do volunteer work or help others in need. While it is true that everyone needs to rest, getting too much rest can stop us from achieving our dreams and goals.

Being active is beneficial as long as we are doing positive things. Working hard with passion is essential, and everyone who works has a purpose. Some people want to achieve their dreams, some need to pay their bills, and others simply love to earn money or support their families. My mother always told me that if I want something, I have to go after it and make it happen. We all need a better future, which is why we must keep moving forward instead of doing nothing.

From a societal perspective, we have to stay active because we need to cover basic expenses like food, housing, bills, and taxes. Therefore, having a job is necessary. However, being active is not just about employment. We can also do other productive things, such as helping people. This kind of work helps us grow as individuals, and whether it is paid or voluntary, doing it makes us valuable members of society.

Ultimately, action is what keeps humanity moving forward and growing. Our dreams and goals are what motivate us to keep going. Jefferson's quote encourages us to reflect on how we spend our lives. While taking a break is important, we must never forget that we have dreams to turn into reality.

It is very important to maintain a positive attitude in life. When we are negative, we do not treat others well, which makes them feel uncomfortable. I agree that having a positive mindset is essential because it helps us secure employment and is highly beneficial both in our daily lives and within our households.

For example, a girl once applied to work at my job, but she only lasted for one day. During her training, she showed a very poor attitude, which is why she could not keep the job. This proves that we must always try to be positive.

In conclusion, if people want to find and keep a job, they must learn to develop a positive attitude. Anyone who is currently negative should try to change, as negativity does not bring good results at work or in life. Ultimately, our attitude determines how we treat the people around us. If we do not want to make others feel sad or uncomfortable because of our behavior, we must always choose to be positive.

Four-day School

Debate between benefits and disadvantages. Resume doing any school activities on a regular five-school-day week and change that to only four days.

To have a four-day school week is an option that has to be adopted not only by some of the business workers but also by each high school and higher education school after seeing these reasons.

That consists of losing ten hours per week, but those missing hours can be recouped by extending the school day by two hours and increasing the time for each class per day. That is an option to increase the attention and time on each class and complete any project or assignment told by your teacher, and if we get the extra two hours, we can get more time with friends and teachers for support between us in any class someone is failing.

Also, we can adopt an option for the fourth day of the extra two hours, used for time in the library; that can be amazing for the student who loves reading, or students who love extra time in sports, or any activity after school.

The fifth day of the week can be used for doctor appointments or any health situations. You know the great excuse for missing classes during regular school time is because the parents write a note explaining we will be absent from some periods of classes. Doing any of those situations during non-regular school time will decrease the students missing any period of class.

Without forgetting the teachers' situations, who are parents at the same time and need one extra day for family time and doing regular activities with their sons if they have them.

Don't forget the situations of seniors, who are in the most difficult situations in their lives, deciding for their future, and they need time for keeping all options from universities and colleges to take the next step, higher education, and considering also a job for the weekends. Also about freshmen, who are the children from middle school, they are in the situation of needing understanding of extra activities in high school, changed from their last routine.

Another option for a Friday or Monday free day can be used for community service, with permission of parents and some supervision of some adults. Any student who wants to participate in this can go and help clean up streets and rivers or any help in relation to community service. Also, the schools can create a program that consists of getting many big companies who want to help students find a job on this new free day, and maybe part-time on the weekend.

Considering:

Only a four-day school week, forgetting about the fifth day of school (No coming for a little time for five days, use the full time on four days)

Three free days per week (use this extra time for family or friends' meetings, anything you and your parents want)

No waking up on Friday mornings or maybe Monday mornings (depends on the decision of the school about which day is going to be the third free day; use time to rest and complete responsibilities)

This idea may not be convenient for students with part-time jobs, because following this model of extending the school day by two hours will decrease the students' timesheets, even though everyone in this situation can use the fifth school day, which will be free, for a full-time job and get three full-time jobs.

Always remember: BEING IN TWO DIFFERENT ACTIVITIES PER DAY CAN BE HARD AND EXHAUSTING. Going to school then going to work is exhausting because you don't have time to rest. But, if you get only four school days, even though the school increases by two hours, you will have time after school to rest and do any project or homework, and use the other three days for any job you think is convenient.

Knowing the disadvantages, there also remain the solutions and benefits for each disagreement on this project, because there are more benefits than disadvantages for more than 90 percent of the students.

After mentioning all points, considering the benefits, disadvantages, and solutions to that for a four-day school week, I willingly conclude with "Everyone needs three days free from school and just four days in school." Even if any student's situation is different for using this free day, whether staying at home, family routines, helping with home routines, working, or studying. And considering that everyone agrees with everything in this document, we all together will have the power to fight for this new right for high school and college students. WITH THE SAME POWER, TOGETHER FOR A NEW RIGHT.

The debate between the benefits and disadvantages of a four-day school week is highly relevant today. Transitioning to a four-day schedule is an excellent option that high schools and universities should adopt, just as some businesses have already done.

Although this change means losing ten hours of school per week, we can easily recover this time. By extending each school day by two hours, classes will be longer. This extra time allows students to focus better, complete projects assigned by teachers, and collaborate with classmates. It also provides a great opportunity to get extra help from teachers and peers in subjects where someone might be struggling.

Furthermore, some of these extra two hours during the four school days could be dedicated to activities like studying in the library, practicing sports, or participating in other after-school programs. This is perfect for students who love reading or want to stay active.

Having a fifth day off would also be highly beneficial for scheduling medical appointments. Currently, the main reason students miss classes is because parents have to write notes explaining their absence for doctor visits. If we schedule these appointments on our day off, student absenteeism during regular class hours will decrease significantly.

We must also consider the teachers. Many of them are parents who need an extra day to spend quality time with their own children and manage their household responsibilities.

This schedule is particularly helpful for high school seniors and freshmen. Seniors face the stressful task of planning their futures, researching colleges, and looking for weekend jobs. They need this extra time to make important decisions. Meanwhile, freshmen, who are transitioning from middle school, need extra time to adapt to their new high school routines and participate in extracurricular activities.

The free day, whether it is Monday or Friday, can also be used for community service. Under parental permission and adult supervision, students can volunteer to clean up streets and rivers or help the community in other ways. Additionally, schools could partner with local businesses to help students find part-time jobs or internships on these free days.

In short, this system means attending school for four full days and enjoying a three-day weekend. Students will not have to wake up early on Friday or Monday morning, depending on which day is chosen as the day off. This extra time can be used to rest, spend time with family, or catch up on personal responsibilities.

Some might argue that this schedule is inconvenient for students with part-time jobs, as longer school days leave less time for work during the week. However, having three full days off actually allows these students to work longer shifts on their free days. Juggling school and work on the same day is exhausting because there is no time to rest. With a four-day week, students can focus on school during the week, have time to relax and do homework, and use the three free days for their jobs.

In conclusion, the advantages of a four-day school week clearly outweigh the disadvantages for the vast majority of students. Everyone deserves a three-day weekend to rest, study, work, or spend time with family. Since this change would benefit almost everyone, students should stand together and advocate for this new right in high schools and colleges. Together, we have the power to make this change happen.

Imagine spending your time on activities that bring you joy, make you feel comfortable, and help you realize your potential in life. Many people believe that students should be allowed to choose their own elective classes in school. This freedom of choice is essential because it helps students discover their true passions, develop valuable skills, find unique opportunities, and prepare for a successful future.

It is incredibly important for students to select the electives they actually want to study. If they are forced into classes they have no interest in, they will likely become unmotivated and lazy. This lack of interest often leads to skipping classes, which results in poor grades. When students get bad grades, they become frustrated and lose all motivation to try. Eventually, they might give up entirely and fail to earn enough credits to graduate. Without a high school diploma, they cannot attend college or secure a good job. In the worst-case scenario, unemployment can even lead to homelessness. Therefore, letting students choose their own electives is crucial for their academic success and future well-being.

Everyone possesses unique talents, and elective classes are the perfect way for students to discover them. When students take classes in subjects they are naturally good at, they enjoy going to school, earn better grades, and easily get their graduation credits. Furthermore, developing these skills opens up many future career opportunities, as employers are always looking for talented individuals. For instance, a student who excels in a drama elective might be hired by a production company, become a famous actor, and earn a lot of money. Developing multiple skills through different electives gives students a significant advantage in the job market and prepares them for various life experiences.

Preparing for the future is vital for young people. By taking electives they genuinely love, students can build a solid foundation for life after high school and college, which is when adulthood truly begins. Having these practical skills makes the transition to adult life much easier. Although they will still face difficult and challenging times, the skills they learned in school will help them overcome these obstacles. Ultimately, electives allow students to pursue their dreams, find their true purpose in life, and reach the destinations they desire.

On the other hand, some people argue that electives should not be required at all. They believe that students may lack the motivation to participate seriously and might just treat these classes as a joke.

The famous writer Ralph Waldo Emerson once said that staying true to yourself in a world that constantly tries to change you is a massive achievement. Today, our actions and attitudes define who we are. Many people believe that going out of your way to help others—like doing tasks at school or work that are not officially your job—shows a kind heart and makes a real difference. I agree with this idea because when you are authentic, people notice your unique qualities. Even if you do not succeed at first, staying true to yourself helps you stand out. There are three main reasons why being yourself is so important: it encourages others to follow your example, it inspires the people around you, and your achievements can change how others think.

First of all, being yourself is essential because it motivates others to behave the same way, especially when you go the extra mile. This happens when you assist someone even though it is not your duty. For instance, if you help a classmate solve a difficult math equation at school, you are doing something extra. Technically, explaining the lesson is the teacher's responsibility, not yours. However, by choosing to help, you show your true character, and this positive action makes other students want to copy your helpful behavior.

Secondly, living authentically allows you to become a source of inspiration for everyone around you, whether at home, in your neighborhood, at school, or at church. For example, if your neighbors see you keeping your yard clean or helping others by cutting their grass, you become a positive role model. This simple act of kindness can motivate them to improve their own surroundings and help one another, fulfilling your goal of being an inspiration to your community.

Finally, being true to yourself can change the mindset of the people around you. When others witness your personal progress, they might wonder how you achieved your goals. This gives you the opportunity to share your journey and show them that if you can succeed, they can do it too. For example, families come in all shapes and sizes; some struggle with low wages, while others own successful businesses. If you are the kind of person who supports your family, you spread hope and positive energy, proving to them that progress is always possible.

In conclusion, as Emerson suggested, humans constantly strive to do extra things to achieve great results in life. A large portion of the population chooses to act this way because they understand the value of helping others. Ultimately, the world benefits from this positive message. By staying true to ourselves and going the extra mile, our achievements can serve as a powerful example and a lasting inspiration for everyone around us.

A homework club provides the encouragement they need, proving that every student has the potential to succeed and complete their tasks when they have the right support.

Many people believe that students do not put enough effort into their work, but I disagree. Students understand that real achievement is built on self-esteem and hard work. In my opinion, we must look to the future. While some people only live in the present moment without understanding the deeper meaning of life, students know that achieving goals is not easy. Truth and reality are the most important foundations in life, and without them, our lives would be completely different.

To succeed, students must have self-confidence. There is a difference between being confident and having confidence. Being confident means you are sure of your own skills and opinions, while confidence is a strong trust in someone or something. Students have a lot of confidence in their ability to learn. Even though they are often ordered to learn—meaning they are strongly told to acquire new knowledge and skills—they do so because they want to become the best at what they do.

An achievement is something successful that you finish through hard work and skill, which gives you a great feeling of satisfaction. However, we should not lower the quality of our lives just by working constantly. I believe that life must offer opportunities to enjoy every single moment. Yes, we have to work hard, but we must also spend time with our families. We cannot let our jobs consume us; we need to stop for a moment, appreciate life, and plan for the future.

What exactly is the future? It is a time that is further ahead of us. But we should not build a future that is only about professional success and making money. There are differences between a profession, an occupation, and employment. While employment is simply a job you do to earn money, a profession requires special training and a high level of education. We must make sure our future is not just about earning a living, but about finding real meaning in what we do.

A career is a series of jobs in a specific field that brings more responsibility over time, like a distinguished career in medicine. This is different from a trade, which usually involves working with your hands and requires practical training. Currently, many students do not have a career or even a job because employers believe they do not have enough experience.

Experience means living through things and learning from both success and failure. Even though students might lack this, they inspire me because they possess sincerity. Sincerity is the quality of being honest and really meaning what you say. Students are honest about their abilities, and they have a very good point of view that we should respect.

Furthermore, students always take precautions. A precaution is an action you take to avoid danger or problems in the future, like locking away valuables or preparing for emergencies. When situations become very serious, students are not afraid to implore others for help, showing that they care deeply about doing things correctly.

They also understand the importance of their future work. In the workplace, tolerance is essential. Tolerance means accepting other people's opinions and behaviors, even when you do not agree with them. Unfortunately, some people show intolerance. Students know that they must work together, combining their efforts to achieve better results.

Many people lack compassion and do not consider the difficulties that students face. We should think carefully about this issue. Instead of being angry at students for their lack of experience, we should show them respect. Students are intelligent, and they do not feel insecure. They have the security and confidence needed to succeed, and this is why I support them.

In my opinion, it is essential for people to make their own decisions by following their personal instincts and ideas. We must have confidence in ourselves because if we do not believe in our own abilities, it is impossible for anyone else to trust us.

To begin with, making independent choices allows people to trust their own minds. When we rely on our own thoughts, we do not need to constantly ask others for their opinions. For instance, when writing an essay, believing in our own ideas means we can create original work instead of copying from other people or the internet.

Furthermore, following our instincts helps us handle difficult situations on our own. When a problem arises, we do not have to wait for someone else to come and solve it. Instead of constantly searching for external guidance, self-confidence allows us to find solutions independently.

Additionally, our self-belief directly affects how others perceive us. For example, if you have to give a presentation in front of your teacher but lack confidence, the teacher will likely doubt your abilities too. This can negatively impact your grade, especially if you constantly look to the teacher for reassurance instead of presenting with certainty.

In conclusion, I strongly believe that people must trust themselves before they look to others for help. If you do not have faith in yourself, nobody else will believe in you either. Ultimately, we should all listen to our own voices first, because relying only on other people's opinions reduces our own self-worth.
